name: Molexar
reason: Not a rename or transfer: the authenticated GitHub API (which follows renames) returns 404, the owner's 5 public repos include neither Molexar nor Fragment-SELFIES, and GitHub repo searches plus PyPI JSON lookups (molexar, fragment-selfies) found no official relocation. The repo was reachable in the local 2026-09-11 link audit (evidence/link_audit.tsv line 1712), so it went offline between 2026-09-11 and today; deleted versus made private cannot be told apart. The authors were still active afterwards: they had renamed the HF checkpoints by 2026-09-11 (molexar-10m-base -> molexar-1-10m-pt, molexar-10m-omni -> molexar-1-10m-it; card commit 'update PT model name' that day), added ModelScope mirrors on 2026-09-19 and updated molexar.com that day, yet the paper, both cards and the site still link the 404 repo. The weights stay public, ungated and MIT, but the cards require installing the Molexar and Fragment-SELFIES repos, and config.json declares a custom model_type 'molexar' with no remote-code mapping. Without the withdrawn code the checkpoints cannot be loaded and their Fragment-SELFIES output cannot be decoded to SMILES; the third-party torch-molecule wrapper also installs from the dead URL. A co-author account (yiyanliao) has a single-commit MIT snapshot, but no official source names it, so it is a lead and not a replacement. Decision: reversible HOLD (artifact), following the ALICE precedent of 2026-09-11. The ID stays reserved; the held record uses the renamed HF IDs and adds the official ModelScope mirrors. Alternative for the integrator: the weights alone still meet the 'released weights' bar, so the record could instead stay displayed as verified_with_limits with the GitHub link dropped and status 'Public MIT weights (ungated); official code offline since Sept 2026, required to load and decode'. I judged that optimistic because the documented reuse route is broken. Integration note: audit_source/source point to evidence/refresh-2026-10-10/candidate_decisions.json, which must exist for the validator; remove the record from models_final.json and add it to records_under_review.json (one store only).

name: UMA
reason: FAIR Chemistry moved its documentation site: https://fair-chem.github.io/ now meta-refreshes to https://facebookresearch.github.io/fairchem, the fairchem repository's homepage field names https://facebookresearch.github.io/fairchem/, and the README links docs on that host. The same 'UMA Models - FAIR Chemistry Documentation' page is live at https://facebookresearch.github.io/fairchem/uma/ (200). The old deep path does not redirect, so a plain host swap is the fix. Licence/access re-check against the current facebook/UMA card: gated='manual' (contact-sharing and approval; gate collects country and IP location); licence 'other' = FAIR Chemistry License v1 (last updated May 14, 2025) with an incorporated Acceptable Use Policy; the card says models are usable commercially and non-commercially and are not offered in comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions, China, Russia or Belarus; fairchem code is MIT (LICENSE.md). The existing wording was accurate but vague; the proposed status adds the MIT code licence, the manual gate, the licence version and the named exclusions. noncommercial=false stays correct: the licence grants royalty-free use with no non-commercial clause, and the restrictions are AUP-based. All row claims were re-checked (paper v2, io charge/spin/task inputs, domains), so verified moves to 2026-10-10 with date_modified 2026-10-10. Checkpoints now include uma-s-1p2p1 (latest small) and uma-m-1p1; no record field needs a version. Integration note: audit_source points to evidence/refresh-2026-10-10/candidate_decisions.json, which must exist.

proposed_change.audit_note_append: Boltz-2 emits confidence scores and an ensemble binder probability; official docs make no calibration claim, and an independent prospective Mac1 study (bioRxiv v4, Sept 2026) applied post-hoc calibration to affinity values.

reasons: Lane rule not met: a calibrated-uncertainty note may be added only if a primary source shows the model itself outputs calibrated uncertainty/confidence. No primary source does. docs/prediction.md and README.md contain zero occurrences of 'calibrat'; the Boltz-1 PMC full text has none; the Boltz-2 technical report's only occurrence is 'calibrated ensembling strategy' (Appendix B.5.2), a molecular-weight correction of the mean affinity regression fitted on a holdout set, not a probability-calibration or reliability claim. The proposal is a negative caveat plus a third-party evaluation, which this lane does not authorise.

Sub-claim 'Boltz-2 emits confidence scores and an ensemble binder probability' is CONFIRMED (prediction.md lines 183-184, 231-242), but on its own it does not correct any existing record claim; io already reads 'structure +/- affinity'.

Sub-claim 'official docs make no calibration claim' is literally true for docs/README but would mislead: the official Boltz-2 technical report does use 'calibrated' (for affinity-regression ensembling), so a reader could misread the note.

Sub-claim about the Mac1 study is only partly confirmed: v4 dated 2026-09-21 exists (bioRxiv API) and the abstract says Boltz-2 affinity 'after calibration' had lower MAE than a baseline. 'Post-hoc' is an inference the abstract does not state. 'Independent' is not established from the abstract alone: no Boltz authors appear in the author list (corresponding author J. S. Fraser, UCSF), but competing interests and funding were not checked and the full text was not read.
Proposal sources carried empty excerpts, and the cited GitHub blob URL returned HTTP 503 to a direct fetch today (the same file is 200 via raw.githubusercontent.com and the GitHub contents API).

Main text, Methods and Supplementary Information confirm: deep ensemble of 5 models, uncertainty = 1 - max(p), higher uncertainty for incorrect and absent/novel cell types, evaluated by ROC-AUC separation (0.782 correct-vs-absent; 0.891 correct-vs-incorrect). Zero hits for 'calibrat', 'Brier', 'expected calibration', 'reliability diagram' in the Europe PMC full text and the Supplementary Information PDF.
rejected_proposals.reason_rejected: Fails the lane gate: a calibrated-uncertainty note may be added only if a primary source shows the model itself outputs calibrated uncertainty/confidence. The sources show uncertainty output and its ROC-AUC separation, with no calibration evaluation, so the gate is not met. The current record already states the mechanism accurately ('scRNA-seq cell expression -> cell-type label (with deep-ensemble uncertainty)'; use_cases 'uncertainty-aware labeling') and claims no calibration, so nothing in it is wrong. The proposed text is a full sentence, beyond the 'short clause' limit. Applying it would also force a full re-verification and re-dating for a non-corrective, precision-only addition.
rejected_proposals.if_reviewer_overrides: If the orchestrator still wants the caveat, a verified short clause for audit_note would be: 'uncertainty = 1 - max ensemble probability (5 models); separation reported by ROC-AUC, no calibration metric'. Today's evidence supports it (Methods + SI Fig. 4), but the checkpoint-host limit below would then require audit_state verified_with_limits.

terms.note: CORRECTION NEEDED. Code: Apache-2.0 (GitHub license API; README says 'This codebase is released under the Apache License 2.0'). Data: the Drive folders carry no BEACON-level licence. However, the claim that the data have 'no stated licence' is incomplete. Paper Appendix A.10 Table 22 gives author-stated terms for each source dataset. These include 'Research Purpose Only' (tmRDB, SRPDB, within bpRNA-1M secondary structure), 'MIT & Non Commerical' (StructImpute) and 'Non Commerical' (OpenVaccine/Kaggle, the Degradation task). Other components are GPLv3 (SpliceAI), MIT, Apache-2.0, CC0, public domain or GEO. The redistributed task data therefore include NC/research-only material. Under the rule, noncommercial must be TRUE, not false. The BEACON-B checkpoints on Drive have no stated licence, so all rights are reserved by default. The re-hosted third-party checkpoints keep their original terms. No gating and no sign-in were needed to view the folders. The component licences were taken from the paper and not re-checked at each upstream source.

identity.note: Paper, repository and archive are the same work and author-endorsed. Crossref lists the PLOS Comput Biol article (published 2025-01-07, Greenman, Amini, Yang). The bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2023.04.17.536962 is-preprint-of that DOI. The paper's Data Availability names github.com/microsoft/protein-uq and the Zenodo concept DOI. The README cites the PLOS article. Release v0.0.2's body is the PLOS URL. Zenodo record 14756563 (concept 10.5281/zenodo.7839141) has the same three creators and isSupplementTo the PLOS DOI. The ICLR 2022 MLDD workshop page has the same title. Not a duplicate: no baseline name, alias, normalized name or URL matches protein-uq, the PLOS/bioRxiv DOIs, the Zenodo DOI or FLIP. Not a fork and not archived.

scope.note: This is not a foundation model and not a dataset or leaderboard. It is the reproducibility code for one benchmarking study. Its object of evaluation is uncertainty heads: Bayesian ridge regression (BRR), a Gaussian process (GP) and five CNN variants, all trained from scratch. It does not evaluate pretrained models. The only pretrained model is frozen, mean-pooled ESM-1b, used as one of two input representations next to one-hot. The data are 8 of the 15 FLIP tasks copied from the FLIP repo, so there is no new dataset. There is no leaderboard, and only 2 commits exist. In train_all.py the representation is hard-coded to choices ['ohe','esm'], so adding another pretrained model needs code changes. Every displayed benchmark record evaluates foundation-model-class models (e.g. ProteinGym, PFMBench, PXMeter, KinConfBench); admitting a UQ-methods study would widen the benchmark boundary, which MAINTENANCE.md says not to do ("curated, not a paper feed"). The proposal's reason ("directly relevant to the ELIXIR-CZ use case") argues relevance to a use case, not scope eligibility. Classified HOLD (scope), not reject, because the catalogue does hold evaluation toolkits (PXMeter) and the boundary for method-comparison benchmarks is a curator policy call.

artifact.note: The claimed artifacts exist. On GitHub: MIT code, environment.yml, notebooks including example.ipynb, and data/aav, data/gb1 and data/meltome zipped splits (copied from FLIP). The Zenodo v0.0.2 archive is open (microsoft/protein-uq-v0.0.2.zip, 140,174,155 bytes; not downloaded). The GitHub releases v0.0.1 (2023-04-17) and v0.0.2 (2025-01-28) have no assets. Nothing trained is released: no UQ model checkpoints, no ESM embeddings (data/embeddings is a symlink into a separate FLIP clone) and no committed results (src/models/results holds only .gitkeep). To reproduce the ESM runs you need the FLIP repo plus the 7.3 GB ESM-1b checkpoint. The repo has been static since the January 2025 tag; its two commits were authored in April 2023.

terms.note: Code is MIT (GitHub licence API, LICENSE 'Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation'). The Zenodo archive is mit-license and open. The paper is CC BY 4.0 (Crossref). Data: the copied FLIP splits sit in the MIT repo without their own licence file. data/README only points to FLIP. FLIP's per-landscape READMEs (copied into protein-uq) state that the modified splits fall under AFL-3.0. Upstream sources: the AAV raw data repository 'doesn't feature a license'; the GB1 eLife data are CC BY 4.0; the Meltome atlas authors stated 'No need for licenses'. The FLIP repo licence is AFL-3.0. The ESM-1b code repository (facebookresearch/esm) is MIT and archived; terms specific to the weight files were not checked separately. There is no gating and no non-commercial term, so noncommercial=false is correct. The proposed status line is accurate but should also say that no trained models, embeddings or leaderboard are released, and that the AAV source data carry no licence.

urls.note: All proposed URLs resolve and show what their labels claim. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1012639 redirects to the PLOS article (200; title matches; page links the repo). https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2023.04.17.536962v1 returns 200 and the title matches. https://github.com/microsoft/protein-uq returns 200. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7839141 resolves to https://zenodo.org/records/14756563 (200; v0.0.2). The source https://zenodo.org/api/records/7839141 redirects to /api/records/14756563 (200). https://iclr.cc/virtual/2022/8620 returns 200 (MLDD workshop poster). https://github.com/J-SNACKKB/FLIP returns 200. The Europe PMC fullTextXML returns 200.

text.note: Three claims are inflated or misleading. (1) use_cases says 'calibration assessment under domain shift (including Meltome thermostability)'. The paper uses Meltome only as Meltome/Random, which it groups under 'random sampling with no domain shift', so there is no Meltome domain-shift result. Some Meltome configurations were also infeasible: BRR and GP on Meltome one-hot. (2) The scope claim 'Benchmark of UQ on pretrained PLM representations' overstates it. One PLM (ESM-1b, mean-pooled) is compared against one-hot, and the one-hot results are in the supplement. (3) The proposal's reason calls it a 'reusable benchmark' and ties inclusion to the ELIXIR-CZ use case, which is not a scope criterion. Correct as stated: the description (seven UQ methods; five CNN variants dropout/ensemble/evidential/MVE/last-layer SVI; AAV, GB1 and Meltome; accuracy, calibration, coverage, width and rank correlation; AL/BO experiments) and year 2022 (ICLR 2022 MLDD workshop page; 2023 preprint; 2025 journal). In the audit_note, the workshop/journal author-name difference is a personal-name detail with no bearing on identity and can be dropped.

identity.note: Closed identity triangle: the bioRxiv full text (10.64898/2026.09.04.749352; corresponding author Seonghwan Seo, KAIST) links github.com/SeonghwanSeo/atlasfold; the repo README links the v2 preprint and the four Hugging Face checkpoints; every fetched hub card cites the same DOI. Repo owner and hub author are the same account (SeonghwanSeo, GitHub profile company KAIST), i.e. the first/corresponding author's personal accounts, not a third-party re-upload. Repo is not a fork (created 2026-05-03, pushed 2026-09-29, releases v1.0.0-v1.0.4, PyPI atlasfold 1.0.4 MIT pointing back to the repo). Not a duplicate: baseline has no AtlasFold/AtlasLM name, alias or URL. Name collisions only: 'ESM Atlas' (bfm-esm-atlas, platform, Biohub structure database) and held 'Atlas (RudolfV successor)' (spatial pathology). AtlasLM is a separately trained model with ESMC architecture, so it is not a renamed version of bfm-esm-c-esm-cambrian.

scope.note: Pretrained, reusable, broader than one task: AtlasLM-3B is a standalone masked protein LM (embeddings, hidden states, attention maps via its own API) and the frozen backbone of AtlasFold (monomer folding) and AtlasFold-M (protein-complex folding). Modality: both 'protein' and 'complex' are defensible. Catalog precedent places PLM-based or single-sequence structure predictors in 'complex' (OmegaFold, ESMFold2, AlphaFold2, AlphaFold-Multimer, OpenFold; only the older ESMFold sits in 'protein'), and the headline artifacts here are folding/co-folding models, so the corrected record uses 'complex'. If the curator prefers to file it with ESM-C/ESMFold, 'protein' is acceptable; nothing else in the record depends on it. Limitation that must be visible: protein chains only, no ligands, DNA or RNA (paper Discussion).

scope.note: Pretrained on ~54.6 ms of aggregated MD (ATLAS, MISATO, MDposit plus BioEmu-release octapeptide/CATH sets) with a frozen Protenix encoder; two released general checkpoints usable on new systems from a structure file. The paper shows reuse beyond the pretraining task (fine-tuning from BioKinema on DD-13M metadynamics beats training from scratch for unbinding), which supports foundation-model scope, consistent with the catalogued BioEmu-1 precedent. Modality 'complex' is defensible: the sqrt checkpoint is trained on and documented for protein-ligand complexes, and the model sits on the Protenix complex stack; caveat that the long-time beta=0.25 checkpoint is single-chain protein only.

identity.note: Paper, repo and hub artifact are one model and author-endorsed. arXiv API id_list=2510.22304 returns 'ODesign: A World Model for Biomolecular Interaction Design' (v1 2025-10-25, v2 2025-10-28, q-bio.BM, first author Odin Zhang). GitHub OTeam-AI4S/ODesign describes itself as the official repository of that paper, is not a fork (fork:false), and its citation block carries eprint 2510.22304. The repo was renamed: gh api on the old path The-Institute-for-AI-Molecular-Design/ODesign resolves to full_name OTeam-AI4S/ODesign, so both URLs are the same repo. The Hugging Face repos still sit under the old org name, which is NOT a third-party re-upload: the official repo's own downloader ckpt/get_odesign_ckpt.sh hard-codes the eight huggingface.co/The-Institute-for-AI-Molecular-Design/{ODesign,OInvFold} resolve URLs (lines 24-31) and the README checkpoint table links the same files. No ODesign entry, alias or URL in baseline/fm_identity.tsv (normalized 'odesign' absent); nearest baseline records are distinct models (bfm-protenix, bfm-proteina-complexa, bfm-pxdesign, bfm-boltzgen). Not a renamed baseline record, not a thin fine-tune of one.

scope.note: In scope: pretrained reusable generative model, four released base checkpoints plus four OInvFold inverse-folding checkpoints, covering several design tasks in one framework (protein-binding protein, ligand-binding protein, atom and motif scaffolding, protein-binding ligand, de-novo and protein-binding RNA/DNA, cyclic peptide, partial diffusion of an existing binder) across protein, small-molecule and nucleic-acid modalities. Not a single-task predictor. Modality 'complex' is correct for this catalog (all-atom interaction/complex design across molecule classes; precedent Proteina-Complexa = complex); the protein-design lane could also claim it, so deduplicate against any protein-lane proposal in this cycle.

artifact.note: Weights exist as claimed; no weights downloaded. HF API The-Institute-for-AI-Molecular-Design/ODesign: private:false, gated:false, created 2025-12-05, siblings list ckpt/odesign_base_prot_flex.pt, odesign_base_prot_rigid.pt, odesign_base_ligand_rigid.pt, odesign_base_na_rigid.pt, each 4324725148 bytes (~4.3 GB). Sequence-design side is also released: HF .../OInvFold (ungated, apache-2.0) holds oinvfold_protein.ckpt, oinvfold_ligand.ckpt, oinvfold_dna.ckpt, oinvfold_rna.ckpt. A third ungated apache-2.0 repo .../ODesign-AB (created 2025-12-18, ab.pt) exists and is not listed in the README table. GitHub releases v0.1.0, v0.1.1, v0.1.2 (Dec 2025) carry no binary assets; weights come from HF only. Repo is active (pushed 2026-07-01, 346 stars). Caveats: inference auxiliary files (components.v20240608.cif + rdkit pickle) and the ~850 GB training archive are distributed via a Google Drive folder that was not inspected, so those routes are unverified; training from scratch is optional and the default initialises from an external ByteDance-hosted protenix_base_default_v0.5.0 checkpoint URL that was likewise not fetched.

terms.note: Code and weights: Apache-2.0, confirmed from two independent places. Repo LICENSE is the Apache 2.0 text with a custom markdown header ('Copyright 2024 ODesign Team and/or its affiliates') plus a human-readable summary, which is why GitHub licence detection returns spdx_id NOASSERTION / 'Other' - the proposal's explanation of that mismatch is accurate and the file itself grants commercial use. README License section states code and model parameters are Apache-2.0. HF cardData.license = apache-2.0 and tags include license:apache-2.0 on all three model repos; gated:false on all three. No NC, academic-only or registration clause found anywhere I fetched; bundled third-party pieces are permissive (license_file_list.md attributes 70 Python files to ByteDance Apache-2.0; ckpt/grnade.h5 8.7 MB from gRNAde, whose repo licence is MIT). noncommercial=false is correct in the 'no NC terms observed' sense. Two unverified terms surfaces, recorded rather than asserted: the Google Drive data folder (no licence seen) and the web server, whose page is a JS shell with no visible terms - so the proposal's status wording 'public web server' overstates what is observable and is corrected.

urls.note: All six proposal URLs re-fetched 2026-10-10 and all resolve, but one label is corrected. https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22304 200 (title and version dates confirmed via the arXiv API, not the HTML). https://github.com/OTeam-AI4S/ODesign 200 (gh api). https://api.github.com/repos/OTeam-AI4S/ODesign/contents/LICENSE 200. https://huggingface.co/api/models/The-Institute-for-AI-Molecular-Design/ODesign 200. https://huggingface.co/The-Institute-for-AI-Molecular-Design/ODesign 200. https://odesign.lglab.ac.cn/ 200, no redirect, <title>ODesign</title>, but the body is a 4.4 kB JS shell: reachability only, nothing about free or unrestricted access, so the 'public web server' label is not supported by what the fetch shows. Added link verified in this task: https://odesign1.github.io/ 200, <title>ODesign | A World Model for Biomolecular Interaction Design</title>. The README's technical-report PDF link and the Google Drive folder were deliberately not fetched/added.

text.note: Description, io and year are factual and free of inflation (the record wisely drops the paper's 'world model' framing; 'builds on Protenix and OpenFold' matches the README Acknowledgements). year 2025 is right (arXiv Oct 2025; repo, HF and releases Dec 2025). Three text corrections: (a) status must not assert a 'public' web server - reworded to reachable server with access terms not inspected; (b) use_cases omits capabilities documented in the README (cyclic-peptide binder design, atom and motif scaffolding, partial diffusion / redesign of an existing binder) - added; (c) audit_note updated with the repo-org rename, the HF-org mismatch and why it is still official, the OInvFold and ODesign-AB checkpoints, the not-inspected Google Drive routes, and the Europe PMC check (query 'ODesign' AND 'biomolecular interaction design' returned hitCount 0 on 2026-10-10, so still an unrefereed preprint). The proposal's own caveats about NOASSERTION and lane deduplication were independently reproduced and kept.

Weights are hosted by the authors on GCS seqnn-share. There is no Hugging Face artifact: the calico HF org has no models, and the HF 'cerberus' hits are unrelated (LLMs, YOLO, patrickjreed/cerberus-neuro-*). identity.note: Paper, repo and hub artifact are the same model and author-endorsed. bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.08.17.744355 v1 (Gao, Sun, Wang, Jiang, Liu; posted 2026-08-21; genomics; corresponding institution Yale University) has a Code availability statement naming github.com/ZjGaothu/RegFM and huggingface.co/Deku21/RegFM. GitHub (not a fork, created 2026-05-12, last push 2026-08-18) and the HF card link to each other. Both LICENSE files read 'Copyright (c) 2026 Zijing Gao' (first author), with the same citation and contact. So Deku21/RegFM is the authors' own upload, not a third-party copy. Normalized name 'regfm' and the repo/hub URLs do not match any of the 444 baseline records or anything in models_final.json/records_under_review.json. The nearest names are distinct models: RegFormer (BGI, singlecell), GET, Decima and scooby.

scope.note: Pretrained in three stages (Methods): MLM on the cis-DNA module (GRCh38, 200 kbp windows), MLM on the trans-regulator module (2,103 TF/CR expression sentences), then cross-context expression prediction on ENCODE (281 cell lines/tissues) and CELLxGENE (663 cell types) pseudo-bulk data. 302M parameters. The paper fine-tunes or probes the backbone for CRE/enhancer classification, promoter bivalency (frozen backbone plus head), dosage sensitivity and Perturb-seq response, and runs zero-shot in silico TF knockout. That is broader than one task. Modality dna matches the displayed precedents GET, Decima and scooby (DNA sequence plus cell context to expression). Limit: the released code implements only the 'genepred' task (src/dataset.py hard-codes processors['genepred']). The downstream fine-tuning pipelines are reported in the paper but not released.

artifact.note: HF API: gated=false, private=false, disabled=false, 269 files, created 2026-07-30, last modified 2026-08-18. There are three checkpoint folders, pretrained_models/{AllProtein,HVG,PBMC}. Each holds model.pth (1,209,925,566 B), modelwhole.pth (1,430,199,403 B), pytorch_model.bin (1,209,942,710 B), optimizer.pt, scheduler, training_args, vocab and an identical config.json. LFS sha256 values differ across the folders, so these are three distinct trained checkpoints, not copies. All config.json files declare finetuning_task 'genepred' (architecture LongBertForGenePrediction7168015wNew), so all are expression-prediction-stage models. No MLM-only module checkpoints are released. The card does not say which folder is which. AllProtein most plausibly matches the paper's full-scale ENCODE all-protein-coding model, and PBMC the README's leave-one-out demo; both are inferences from folder names. Tokenizers (cisDNA BPE, TFCR, Exp) are on the Hub. No preprocessing script, processed input features or demo inputs are released: the notebook has /path/to placeholders for DNA, TF and expression features. No GitHub releases. Weights were not downloaded or loaded.

scope.note: Pretrained 479,195,678-parameter encoder (10 bidirectional Mamba2 blocks + 5 local-attention MoE blocks, graph adapter) trained by masked language modelling plus graph-feature reconstruction on 54.65 Gb from 66 tomato accessions; reusable via embeddings, masked-token prediction and LoRA. Broader than one task; modality 'dna' correct. Limits: single genus; downstream evidence is two genic-region tasks (gene- and CDS-versus-intergenic) in two held-out accessions, run with graph input disabled; PlantDNAMamba beat it in every frozen-probe and LoRA comparison. A single-crop model is in scope by the displayed OneGenome-Rice precedent.

identity.note: Same model across paper, repo and archive. The paper's Code Availability (v1 PDF p.16; v2 PDF p.21) points to github.com/CHNFTQ/Evo2HiC 'including the model weights', released under Apache 2.0. The repo is owned by first author Tangqi Fang (UW PhD student; not a fork; description 'Official implementation of Evo2HiC'), and its README links Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17917912. That Zenodo record was created by Fang (UW, ORCID given) with related identifier isSupplementTo 10.1101/2025.11.18.689171. Not a duplicate of the baseline: no Evo2HiC name or alias exists. It is a separate distilled 3.6M-parameter CNN with its own Hi-C encoder, so it is neither Evo 2 (bfm-evo-2) nor HiCFoundation (bfm-hicfoundation, which shares authors Noble/S. Wang but is a different model and repo). Orca (bfm-orca) is only a comparator. Searching Hugging Face for 'evo2hic'/'Evo2HiC' found no models, so there is no third-party re-upload to worry about.

scope.note: Pretrained via contrastive distillation of Evo 2 (7B) into a 3.6M-parameter CNN sequence encoder aligned to a Hi-C patch encoder (v2 p.3). The released backbone is fine-tuned for several tasks: Hi-C prediction from sequence, Hi-C resolution enhancement (177 DNA Zoo species), and epigenomic prediction for 5 assays. It also provides retrieval embeddings and attribution/motif analysis. That makes it reusable and broader than one task, matching the HiCFoundation/Orca precedent. modality 'dna' fits catalog practice: HiCFoundation (Hi-C only) and Orca are both 'dna'. The authors call it 'multimodal', but both of its modalities are genomic, so 'multimodal' is a defensible alternative but not required.

artifact.note: Zenodo record 17917912 (resource_type Model, access_right open) holds one file, evo2hic_checkpoints.tar.zst, 1,472,514,012 bytes (md5 2cce8919...). Its description lists three groups: pretraining weights, a resolution-enhancement model and an epigenomic-prediction model, each with config files. No fine-tuned Hi-C-from-sequence (Seq2HiC) checkpoint is listed. That task needs fine-tuning from the pretrained checkpoint with the released train/train_CDNA2d_Seq2HiC.py. The archive was not opened (download rule), so its contents are known only from the Zenodo description. The repo has no GitHub releases. The code includes pretraining, fine-tuning, inference and interpretation scripts (last push 2026-07-08).

terms.note: Code: Apache-2.0 (GitHub license API; LICENSE file). Weights: Zenodo licence apache2.0, open and ungated, no sign-in needed to see metadata. The paper's Code Availability also says Apache License 2.0. The vendored imagen_pytorch.py carries an MIT notice adapted from lucidrains/imagen-pytorch. The teacher model Evo 2 (arcinstitute/evo2) is Apache-2.0. Training and evaluation data are public ENCODE/4DN Hi-C, which the repo does not redistribute. The preprint text is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. That licence covers the paper only, not the code or weights, so noncommercial=false is correct; catalog precedent bfm-mgm2 likewise does not derive NC from the preprint licence. The status wording is accurate, but it should name which task-specific models are released.

urls.note: All 3 record URLs resolve. bioRxiv v2 returns 200, but the HTML is abstract-only; the full text came from the v2 PDF (200). github.com/CHNFTQ/Evo2HiC returned a transient 504 twice, then 200 on retry; the gh API returned 200 throughout. zenodo.org/records/17917912 returns 200, and the Zenodo API confirms the title, licence and file. doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17917912 returns 302 to Zenodo.

text.note: Mostly accurate. Year 2025 is correct (v1 posted 2025-11-19, Zenodo published 2025-11-19; v2 posted 2026-10-08, not journal-published). Three corrections: (a) use_cases said 'motif interpretation of 3D genome structure', but the paper attributes Hi-C-conditioned epigenomic predictions to find cell-type-specific motifs (v2 p.9), so the wording is narrowed; (b) the status and use_cases now say that Hi-C-from-sequence needs user fine-tuning, because no Seq2HiC checkpoint is listed in the Zenodo archive description; (c) the description adds the verified 3.6M-parameter size, and the audit_note records the preprint CC BY-NC-ND scope and the paper's Code Availability evidence. identity.note: Paper, repo and hub are one model, all author-run. Preprint (Li & Brixi et al., bioRxiv DOI 10.64898/2026.09.22.753630; v1 dated 2026-09-23, v2 2026-09-24, which adds author Wilkinson) names github.com/garykbrixi/minerva and the two HF checkpoints in its availability statement. Repo owner Garyk Brixi (Stanford) is the second author. The HF cards link back to the repo and cite the same DOI. HF user gbrixi matches the repo and PyPI author (minerva-dna). Nothing named minerva is in the baseline (displayed or held). gLM2, the parent model, is also absent from the baseline and is proposed separately. This is a separately trained derivative, so it is not a rename of gLM2. It is unrelated to the sapienzanlp Minerva text LLMs.

scope.note: Pretrained 650M masked genome language model, continued-pretrained from gLM2 650M for 1.2M steps at 4,096 tokens, then 620k more steps at 8,192 tokens for the 8k variant. The run used a new corpus mix (OMG 25% / GlobDB r226 75%). This is not a thin fine-tune. Reusable through MLM logits, embeddings (hidden states, also used for UMAP in the paper), LoRA/full finetuning scripts and three interaction heads (RNA base pairing, protein contacts, repeats). That makes it broader than one task. Modality dna fits the existing genome-LM records such as gLM (bfm-glm-genomic-language-model). Input is mixed amino-acid plus nucleotide tokens, the same convention as gLM2.

artifact.note: The HF API lists model.safetensors (2,682,488,928 bytes) plus custom modeling code, LICENSE and config in both gbrixi/minerva-mlm and gbrixi/minerva-mlm-8k. Both repos are ungated and public, created 2026-05-26 and last modified 2026-10-08. The two configs differ only in RoPE base (10000 vs 20000), which matches the paper. The 8k card declares base_model gbrixi/minerva-mlm. GitHub has code with Apache-2.0, finetuning scripts and tests, but no GitHub releases. A PyPI package minerva-dna 0.2.2 (Apache-2.0) and an HF Space demo both resolve. Weights were not downloaded.

terms.note: Code is Apache-2.0 (GitHub licence API, LICENSE file). Both checkpoints are Apache-2.0: cardData plus an Apache 2.0 LICENSE file in each HF repo, and gated=false. The PyPI package is Apache-2.0. The parent gLM2_650M is Apache-2.0 and ungated (HF cardData; TattaBio/gLM2 GitHub is Apache-2.0), so no NC terms are inherited. The preprint is CC BY. No new training data is released: the OMG and GlobDB third-party corpora were not checked for terms and are not redistributed here. noncommercial=false is correct for every access route found. identity.note: Paper, repo and hub are one official Tatta Bio release. bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.08.14.607850 (Cornman ... Ovchinnikov, Hwang; corresponding institution Tatta Bio) names huggingface.co/tattabio/gLM2_150M and gLM2_650M and github.com/TattaBio/gLM2; the GitHub repo (TattaBio org, not a fork) links both hub repos and cites the preprint; both hub cards link back to the GitHub repo and cite the same preprint. None of these is a third-party re-upload. Not in the baseline: fm_identity.tsv has no gLM2/tattabio/OMG/607850 row. bfm-glm-genomic-language-model is gLM (Hwang et al., Nat Commun 2024, y-hwang/gLM), a different model: it takes ESM-2 protein embeddings as input under non-commercial terms, while gLM2 takes raw amino-acid and nucleotide tokens and is Apache-2.0. The two share a senior author, so gLM2 is a successor. The catalog keeps successors as separate records (Evo / Evo 2, ESM-2 / ESM3), so do not merge gLM2 into the gLM record as an alias. Duplicate inside this refresh: the DNA lane already accepted gLM2 as bfm-glm2 in Foundation_models/evidence/refresh-2026-10-10/candidate_decisions.json and reviewed_changes.json. This feed-watchlist proposal is the same candidate and must be merged into that one record, not added a second time.

scope.note: Pretrained masked-LM transformer encoder (30% masking, 600k steps, 315B pretraining tokens per the hub card) with reusable public weights. The preprint shows protein and DNA downstream tasks (DGEB), protein-protein interface contacts from co-evolutionary signal (categorical Jacobian), and regulatory syntax in intergenic regions. That is broader than one task. Modality 'dna' is correct and matches gLM, Evo and LucaOne; in this catalog 'multimodal' is used for cross-modal text/molecule models.

artifact.note: Both hub repos are public with gated=false. tattabio/gLM2_650M has model.safetensors of 2,682,482,800 bytes, last committed 2024-09-23. tattabio/gLM2_150M has model.safetensors of 609,855,088 bytes, last committed 2024-09-14. Both carry tokenizer files and custom modeling_glm2.py, so loading needs trust_remote_code. The weights have not changed since September 2024; only the modeling code changed (Feb 2026, init_weights fix). The proposal said the 150M repo was evidenced only by the README link; I verified it directly through the API. Nothing was downloaded or executed.

terms.note: Code: Apache-2.0 (GitHub API licence plus a LICENSE file). Weights: Apache-2.0, declared in the hub cardData and licence tag on both repos; neither hub repo has its own LICENSE file. Training data: the OMG dataset card declares CC BY-SA 4.0, which is share-alike and not NC. No gating, API or server route. noncommercial=false is correct for every artifact the record links. Notes: (a) the preprint text is CC BY-NC (bioRxiv), but that licence covers the paper, not a model artifact; (b) the OMG preprocessing repo github.com/TattaBio/OMG has no licence file, meaning all rights reserved; the record does not link it; (c) derivative Tatta checkpoints are outside this record: gLM2_650M_bgc_decoder and the FlashPPI models are CC BY-NC 4.0, and gLM2_650M_UR50, gLM2_150M_no_prune and gLM2_650M_sae have no licence metadata; (d) I did not review upstream IMG/MGnify data-use terms. Correction: the proposed status left out the data licence, and the access wording rules require data terms to be stated.

identity.note: bioRxiv API and Crossref both resolve DOI 10.64898/2026.09.24.754017: 'EpiZoo: a DNA sequence-aware foundation model for cross-species single-cell epigenomics', Li K., Chen X., ... Jiang R. (Tsinghua), posted 2026-09-29, v1, new results, bioinformatics. The preprint's Code availability names github.com/likeyi19/EpiZoo. The repo owner likeyi19 is 'Keyi Li' (first author; also the pyproject author). The repo is not a fork, was created 2026-06-06 and last pushed 2026-09-17. Its README carries the same title and links the checkpoint, and so does tutorial 01. No Hugging Face artifact was looked for or claimed. The baseline identity TSV has no 'epizoo' name, alias, normalized name or likeyi19 URL. EpiZoo is not a rename of bfm-epiagent. It comes from the same group (Chen X. is the EpiAgent author; Jiang R. is corresponding author on both) and Omni-scATAC includes EpiAgent's pretraining data. But it is a new model: new name, repo, preprint, MoE architecture with a DNABERT-2-derived SEAM sequence encoder, and a human+mouse vocabulary. The preprint benchmarks against EpiAgent as a baseline. The DNA and single-cell discovery lanes both proposed EpiZoo; merge them into one record.

scope.note: This is a pretrained (~2.6B-parameter MoE) scATAC foundation model with one released base checkpoint and documented reuse: embedding extraction (zero-shot and fine-tuned), LoRA/full fine-tuning, annotation, imputation, post-training to new species, mutation scoring and sequence-to-accessibility prediction (7 tutorial notebooks). It covers more than one task. Modality 'singlecell' is correct: the primary input is single-cell chromatin accessibility, and the record sits next to bfm-epiagent. DNA sequence only enters as a token prior, so 'dna' would be wrong.

artifact.note: README 'Model checkpoint' and examples/01_extract_cell_embeddings.ipynb both link Google Drive file pretrained_EpiZoo.pth. The Drive view page returned HTTP 200 without sign-in redirect; title 'pretrained_EpiZoo.pth - Disk Google'; itemJson names the file; isItemTrashed false. The file was not downloaded; size, integrity and any Drive download quota were not checked. The repo has no GitHub Releases. Only the base pretrained checkpoint is linked. No released checkpoints were found for the fine-tuned annotation, EpiZoo-Evo, EpiZoo-Cancer or sequence-prediction variants; users train those with the repo code. The repo bundles small demo/vocabulary files (data/*.h5ad, cCRE index/frequency files). No packaged Omni-scATAC corpus was found. Per the preprint's Data availability section, the source datasets are listed in Supplementary Table 1 (not opened).

terms.note: Code: MIT (GitHub licence API spdx MIT; LICENSE 'Copyright (c) 2026 likeyi19'). The README's License section says 'This project is released under the MIT License'. The checkpoint lives on Google Drive outside the git tree and has no licence of its own, so treat the weights as having no separate weight licence; whether the project-wide MIT statement covers them is not explicit. config/SEAM_config/ holds DNABERT-2 configuration/code files with an Apache-2.0 LICENSE. Not gated; no API/server. The preprint text is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (bioRxiv API + JATS). That covers the paper only, not a model artifact, so noncommercial=false stands. noncommercial=false does not prove the weights carry a permissive licence. The proposed status wording is accurate and only needs alignment with catalog phrasing (cf. bfm-tissueformer, bfm-utrgen).

urls.note: All record URLs return HTTP 200 and show what their labels claim. https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.09.24.754017v1: 200, title matches. https://github.com/likeyi19/EpiZoo: the first two curl attempts returned 504, a third attempt about 20 s later returned 200, and the GitHub API returned 200 throughout. The Google Drive checkpoint view URL, which the lane listed as evidence but not as a record source, returned 200. bioRxiv's citation_publication_date meta reads 2026/01/01 (a placeholder); citation_date is 2026-09-29.

text.note: The facts check out: 2.6B parameters, MoE, ~20.9M cells, cell-sentence tokenization, annotation, imputation, cross-species, somatic mutation, sequence-based prediction, year 2026. Three things need correcting. (1) 'curated multi-species scATAC corpus' overstates the pretraining data. Methods: Omni-scATAC was built 'by manually curating available human and mouse scATAC-seq datasets', and Fig. 1a calls it a 'human-mouse scATAC-seq corpus'. Macaque, zebrafish, fruit fly and maize were reached by post-training only. (2) The io and use_cases read as if the released checkpoint performs annotation and sequence-based prediction directly. In the paper, annotation fine-tunes on a tissue-matched reference, while cancer and sequence prediction are extension models; only the base checkpoint is released. (3) 'somatic-mutation prioritization' should name noncoding mutations and the EpiZoo-Cancer extension. The README and Methods disagree on dataset count (README '42 public datasets'; paper: 46 dataset entries, 42 published plus 10x data); the record avoids that number. The preprint is v1 and not peer reviewed.

scope.note: Pretrained from scratch: ESM-2-style 12-layer encoder, ~87M parameters, masked language modelling at single-nucleotide resolution; Stage 1 = 7,025,323 non-redundant 3' UTRs from 1,715 genomes, Stage 2 = 59,221 UTRs from human, mouse, rat and zebrafish excluded from Stage 1 (total 7,084,544 from 1,719 genomes). Modality rna is correct and matches UTR-LM/UTRGen.

identity.note: Paper, repo and hub artifact are the same model and author-endorsed. bioRxiv API: 'Interaction Profiles as a Universal Language for Generative Molecular Design with ShEPhERD-2', doi 10.64898/2026.09.10.750648, Abeywardane / Walker / Coley, MIT, v1 2026-09-12 and v2 2026-09-16, cc_by. github.com/coleygroup/shepherd2 (owner coleygroup, created 2026-09-10, pushed 2026-09-16) is the official implementation; src/shepherd/loader/checkpoint_manager.py hardcodes HF_REPO_ID = 'kabeywar/shepherd2', so the hub repo is the one the official package pulls. The proposal's caveat that the weights sit on a 'first-author personal hub account' understates the endorsement: https://huggingface.co/api/users/kabeywar/overview gives fullname 'Kento Abeywardane' and org membership 'CRG-MIT' / 'Coley Research Group', and the bioRxiv v2 page itself lists the GitHub, Zenodo and Hugging Face links. Not a third-party re-upload. No duplicate: no 'sheph' match in fm_identity.tsv (400 displayed + 44 held) and no 'shepherd' string anywhere under Foundation_models, so ShEPhERD v1 (Adams et al., ICLR 2025) is not a baseline record being renamed; ShEPhERD-2 is a separate successor with its own paper and weights.

scope.note: Pretrained once and reused: trained on MOSES, 'which contains 1.6 million neutral, drug-like molecules', for '300k optimization steps' (Methods 4.4), with released checkpoints. Breadth comes from conditioning, not retraining: 'We demonstrate the application of a single model' ... 'without task-specific retraining' (abstract), covering bioisosteric fragment merging, dual-target design, selectivity engineering and modality hopping, plus pharmacophore prioritization and substructure constraints. Broader than one task in the catalog's sense and consistent with existing molecule-modality generative records (GenMol, Megalodon, PocketXMol, NExT-Mol). Modality 'molecule' is correct: small-molecule 3D structures, no protein-complex input ('eliminating the need for protein-ligand complex data', Sec. 2.1), so not 'complex'. Limit worth keeping visible: only the MOSES-aq model line is released, i.e. neutral drug-like chemical space.

artifact.note: Weights exist as claimed and were inspected without downloading. HF API (blobs=true) for kabeywar/shepherd2: gated false, private false, disabled false, cardData {'license': 'mit'}, createdAt 2026-09-04, siblings shepherd2/shepherd2-mosesaq-inference.ckpt (25601974 B = 25.6 MB) and shepherd2/shepherd2-mosesaq-resume.ckpt (76486094 B = 76.5 MB) - the sizes in the proposal are right. Hub tree page and a HEAD on the inference checkpoint both returned 200 with 0 bytes transferred. GitHub has no releases (releases?per_page=5 returned an empty array), so the hub is the only weight route; the automatic fetch is verified from code (huggingface_hub.hf_hub_download with the pinned repo id), not by executing the package. Zenodo 22675706 'ShEPhERD-2 Supplementary Data' (2026-09-09) holds moses_aq_hdf5.zip (1.16 GB) plus three evaluation/case-study archives; a newer version of the same concept exists (10.5281/zenodo.22798054, 2026-09-16, same MIT licence, adds shepherd2-moses-input_data.zip), concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22675705. terms.note: Code: MIT, confirmed from the repository licence endpoint (spdx_id MIT, path LICENSE, 'Copyright (c) 2026 Coley Research Group @ MIT'); README section 'License' agrees. Weights: hub card declares license: mit in YAML front matter (raw README.md is front matter only, no LICENSE file and no model description in the card) and the repo is ungated and public - the licence claim rests on card metadata, which is the publisher's own declaration. Data: Zenodo metadata.license.id = 'mit-license' on both the pinned version and the newer one. Paper: CC BY 4.0. No gating, no NC terms, no login on any route, so noncommercial: false is correct; this is a positive MIT declaration on each artifact, not an absence of terms. urls.note: Every URL in the proposed record was re-fetched and shows what its label says. https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.09.10.750648v2 -> 200, title and authors as claimed, 'It is made available under a CC-BY 4.0 International license.', footnotes list the GitHub, Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.22675706) and Hugging Face links. https://github.com/coleygroup/shepherd2 -> API 200, MIT, official. https://huggingface.co/kabeywar/shepherd2 -> 200, ungated, two checkpoints. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22675706 -> 302 to the Zenodo DOI page, record content confirmed through the Zenodo API. One label correction: the Zenodo deposit is titled 'ShEPhERD-2 Supplementary Data' and contains evaluation and case-study archives alongside the training HDF5, so the label 'Training data' overstates it. Minor divergence recorded, not an error: the repo README cites the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22675705 while the preprint and the proposal cite version DOI ...706; the concept DOI now redirects to version 22798054.

text.note: Mostly factual, three fixes. (1) 'A single released checkpoint' - two checkpoint files are released (inference and training-resume) for one MOSES-aq model; reworded to 'a single model checkpoint (MOSES-aq)'. (2) use_cases 'pocket-free structure-based design' is a phrase the paper never uses; the supportable statements are 'representing the target pocket only through its bound ligand interactions' (Discussion) and 'despite not conditioning on pocket geometry directly' (Sec. 2.3), and Methods 4.5.2 describes a 'pocket-conditioned setting' as an evaluation variant, so 'pocket-free' as a product claim is too strong; reworded to ligand-interaction-conditioned design without pocket-geometry conditioning. (3) audit_note ownership caveat corrected (hub account is a Coley Research Group org member, and the preprint links the hub page itself) and training corpus added. Everything else holds: diffusion model (ShEPhERD = Shape, Electrostatics and Pharmacophores Explicit Representation Diffusion), year 2026, io direction, the four design applications, and the xTB requirement. The proposed record was also missing six schema-required fields (id, date_added, canonical, verified, audit_priority, audit_source), supplied below; id and audit_source path are maintainer assignments to confirm.

identity.note: bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.09.03.747733 (v1 2026-09-07, v2 2026-09-08; bioRxiv API; corresponding author K. Kalogeropoulos, DTU; author list includes InstaDeep Ltd and DTU affiliations) is titled 'Learning from tandem mass spectra at scale with a self-supervised foundation model for proteomics'. Its Code availability section names github.com/instadeepai/InstaNovo-FM and says weights are in that repository's Releases. The repo (owner instadeepai, not a fork, not archived) calls itself 'The official code repository for InstaNovo-FM' and cites the same DOI; the v0.1.0 release notes cite the same DOI. Endorsement runs both ways. No HF model repo exists for InstaNovo-FM (HF model search 'instanovo' returns only InstaDeepAI/instanovo-v1.x and instanovoplus, i.e. the earlier supervised de novo sequencer line), so no third-party re-upload was involved. No 'instanovo' string in fm_identity.tsv, models_final.json or records_under_review.json; nearest InstaDeep records (Nucleotide Transformer, AgroNT, SegmentNT, ChatNT) are unrelated DNA/multimodal models. Not a duplicate or rename. The earlier InstaNovo (de novo peptide sequencing) is a separate, task-specific model and is not in the catalog.

scope.note: Pretrained (self-supervised masked reconstruction of MS/MS spectra without peptide-sequence labels), reusable (frozen embeddings loaded via from_pretrained), and broader than one task: paper and README show de novo sequencing, database-free identification/rescue, PTM and glycan probes, and run-level classification from the same encoder. Not a single-task predictor or thin fine-tune. Modality 'protein' is a curation choice, since the input is peptide fragmentation spectra and the catalog has no spectra modality; bottom-up proteomics maps more closely to 'protein' than to 'molecule' or 'multimodal'. Accept 'protein' and keep the routing caveat in audit_note.

artifact.note: GitHub release v0.1.0 (published 2026-09-08, not draft, not prerelease) lists eight .ckpt assets: five pretrained encoders (instanovo-fm-v0.1.0 = the published model, three LCFM factorial ablations, one MCFM 40M baseline; ~358 MB or ~160 MB each) and three de novo sequencers (fine-tuned, frozen-encoder, and a from-scratch no-pretraining control; ~691 MB each). src/instanovo_fm/models.json maps each id to its release download URL. A HEAD request on instanovo-fm-v0.1.0.ckpt returned 302 to GitHub release-asset storage; nothing was downloaded or executed. Embeddings dataset InstaDeepAI/InstaNovo-FM-embeddings: gated=false, parquet configs 100k and 1M, created 2026-09-09. Pretraining corpus InstaDeepAI/InstaNovo: gated=false, 46,209 files. The unlabelled ACFM tier (~1.63B spectra) is not redistributed.

terms.note: Code: Apache-2.0 (GitHub license API, LICENSE.md). Checkpoints: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (README License table line 353 and the v0.1.0 release notes). Embeddings dataset: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (README line 356; HF cardData.license cc-by-nc-sa-4.0). Corpus dataset InstaDeepAI/InstaNovo: EMBL-EBI terms of use (README line 355; HF cardData license 'other', license_name embl-ebi-terms-of-use). Corpus-production code on Figshare is stated in the README as CC BY 4.0; I did not fetch the Figshare record (not cited in the record). No gating on any route. The preprint itself is cc_by_nc (bioRxiv API). noncommercial=true is correct because the weights and embeddings carry NC terms. The proposed status is accurate; the correction only spells out what the eight checkpoints are and states the ungated, ACFM-not-redistributed facts.

urls.note: All proposed URLs fetched 2026-10-10: bioRxiv v2 page 200 (doi.org resolves to it); github.com/instadeepai/InstaNovo-FM 200; releases/tag/v0.1.0 200 and API shows the eight assets; huggingface.co/datasets/InstaDeepAI/InstaNovo-FM-embeddings 200 with matching API metadata. Added source huggingface.co/datasets/InstaDeepAI/InstaNovo 200. bioRxiv JATS XML returned an empty body to curl; full text was read through WebFetch of the .full page.

text.note: Inflated training-data claim. The proposed description says the model was 'trained by physics-aware masked reconstruction on a corpus of 1.63 billion tandem mass spectra'. The abstract says 'We train an encoder-only transformer on the annotated tier', and README lines 113-114 say the released checkpoints are trained on LCFM (184.6M PSMs) with one MCFM model, while ACFM (~1.63B) is not released and was not used for the deployed model. The description is corrected to the LCFM tier. Minor fixes: io changed from 'task heads' to the actual routes (decoder for sequencing, embedding nearest-neighbour retrieval for identification, aggregated embeddings for run classification); PTM/glycan detection added to use_cases (README and paper); parameter count (~89.5M) added from the README model table. Year 2026 correct.

identity.note: Preprint (bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.08.23.746565, posted 2026-08-25, corresponding author Daisuke Kihara, Purdue) names both https://github.com/kiharalab/Prot-LAMBDA and https://huggingface.co/KiharaLab/ProtLAMBDA in its Code Availability section; the HF card links back to the GitHub repo. HF org KiharaLab = 'Kihara Bioinformatics Laboratory' (not HF-verified, but author-endorsed by the paper). GitHub repo is not a fork, created 2026-08-19. No baseline match for prot-lambda/protlambda/lambdafold/kiharalab; the only name collision is bfm-lambda (LAMBDA prophage benchmark, leannmlindsey/LAMBDA), which is unrelated.

scope.note: Reusable pretrained PLM: ESM2-650M with the top 11 of 33 layers further trained on PDB + AlphaFold DB structures using MLM plus inter-residue contact supervision and an added axial-attention pair module. Paper evaluates the frozen embeddings by linear probing on several tasks (secondary structure 3/8-state, disorder, phi/psi, RSA, fold) plus contacts and structure prediction, so it is broader than one task and more than a thin task fine-tune. LambdaFold/RAG are bundled structure-prediction components. Modality 'protein' is correct.

artifact.note: HF API (ungated, public, not disabled) lists ProtLAMBDA.pth (2,615,432,275 B), DistFormer.pth (234,212,436 B), LambdaFold.pth (8,499,874 B), RAG.pth (17,942,842 B); not downloaded. Example notebooks load exactly these four filenames via load_state_dict. Caveats for the audit note: the GitHub README wrongly tells users to download parameters from Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.21984993, which holds only predictions (contact maps, distograms, predicted-structure zips, CC BY 4.0); three of four notebooks hardcode internal /net/kihara/... paths. No GitHub releases. RAG demo consumes a precomputed template pickle (pseudo_beta, valid_mask); the repo contains no template-search/retrieval tooling.

terms.note: Code: GPL-3.0 (GitHub API license + LICENSE file). Weights: HF cardData license gpl-3.0 and card text 'licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0'; the card's 'see the LICENSE file' link returns 404 (no LICENSE file in the HF repo), so hub terms are declared by metadata and card text only. Ungated. Preprint text itself is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (applies to the manuscript, not the model). Zenodo predictions CC BY 4.0. Wording tension: the preprint says code and weights are 'freely available for academic use' and the README invites contact for 'a different license, for example, for commercial use'; the granted licence is still GPL-3.0, which does not bar commercial use. noncommercial=false is consistent with catalog precedent (bfm-utr-lm, GPL-3.0, nc=false), but the status must disclose the academic-use wording. Upstream components verified: facebookresearch/esm MIT, aqlaboratory/openfold Apache-2.0.

identity.note: arXiv 2608.14414 (Qadri, Hiller, Blanke, ..., Kirste, Becker; Univ. Rostock / Marburg; cs.LG; v1 2026-08-14) links github.com/bckrlab/cytobert and a code snapshot, data artifacts and Docker image in Appendix 0.A. Repo is original (not a fork), created 2026-07-10, release v1.0 'REHMED@ECML' by chillerb. Zenodo 21291131 (data+weights), 21298697 (Docker) and 21299708 (code snapshot) list the paper's first/second/last authors as creators and sit in the 'bckrlab' Zenodo community. Official, author-released; no third-party re-upload; no Hugging Face artifact found (HF search 'cytobert' returned []). Baseline identity TSV (444 records) has no CytoBERT, cytometry/CyTOF, ImmuneFM, CyMAE or bckrlab entry, so not a duplicate or rename. Within this run the same model is also proposed by the singlecell lane (discovery/singlecell.json candidates[4]); merge to one record.

scope.note: Self-supervised masked expression-bin pretraining of a Transformer encoder (d=128, 6 layers, 8 heads) over a 220-marker shared vocabulary on about 50M cells from 15 of 18 curated ImmPort CyTOF datasets, released as a reusable pretrained checkpoint with fine-tuning code. Panel-agnostic encoder for transfer across studies, so broader than one task, but the paper evaluates only sample-level classification (7 datasets) and reports no significant difference from baselines (Friedman p=0.093). Repository tutorials add cell-type classification and reference mapping from CLS embeddings, but the cell-classification tutorial loads a separate cell_tasks checkpoint (epoch 100, own 530-byte vocab) and Google Drive data, not the pretrained epoch-50 model. Modality singlecell (single-cell protein cytometry) is correct. Small model; accept as verified_with_limits.

identity.note: Paper (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.06.04.656517, Li, Wu, Zhu, Feng, Ye, Wang; v1 2025-06-05, latest v3 2025-08-14, Alibaba Cloud Computing), GitHub GenerTeam/GENERanno (not a fork, MIT) and the four GenerTeam hub repos cross-reference each other: the abstract points to the GitHub repo, and the hub cards cite the paper and the repo. Same organization as the displayed GENERator (bfm-generator), but a different model: GENERanno is a masked-LM encoder (GenerannoForMaskedLM), while GENERator is a generative decoder. 'generanno' does not appear anywhere in the Foundation_models tree or the identity baseline, so this is not a duplicate. Limit: the preprint describes only the prokaryotic model and lists GENERanno-Eukaryote as 'planned'. The eukaryotic base and the eukaryotic annotator are documented only by the README and hub cards ('developmental phase'; 'More technical details are coming soon').

scope.note: The model was pretrained from scratch on 715B bp of prokaryotic DNA with an MLM objective: 500M-parameter encoder, 8192 bp context, single-nucleotide tokens. The authors evaluate it on CDS annotation, pseudogene prediction, taxonomic classification, and the Prokaryotic Gener Tasks (gene fitness, antibiotic resistance, gene classification, taxonomy), and the cards provide reusable embedding extraction. That is broader than one task and not a thin fine-tune. Modality dna is correct.

identity.note: Preprint 10.1101/2025.11.12.688125 (v1 only, 2025-11-13; corresponding author Ali Madani, Profluent Bio Inc.) links to github.com/Profluent-AI/E1, whose README links the three Profluent-Bio/E1-{150m,300m,600m} hub repos; the hub cards point back to the repo. Profluent-AI and Profluent-Bio are the same orgs that host the baseline ProGen3 record. No collision with baseline names, aliases or URLs (e1, profluente1, E1-* not present; only ProGen/ProGen2 and ProGen3 relate to Profluent). E1 is a different model from ProGen3 (masked encoder, not autoregressive generator). Third-party ports exist (alexanderbonnet/e1-jax) but the proposal uses only the official artifacts. Europe PMC and Crossref show no journal version.

scope.note: Pretrained masked protein language model family (150M/300M/600M) trained on ~4 trillion tokens; reusable for embeddings, zero-shot fitness/variant scoring and unsupervised contact-map prediction, in single-sequence or retrieval-augmented mode. Broader than one task; modality protein is correct.

artifact.note: HF API (blobs=true) for all three repos: gated=false, private=false, model.safetensors present (600m 1,282,911,716 B; 300m 548,657,620 B; 150m 308,869,268 B) plus config.json (E1ForMaskedLM). Repo has inference code, cookbooks and scorer/predictor tools; no training code, no training data, no GitHub releases. Retrieval mode needs user-supplied homologs or an A3M MSA (src/E1/msa_sampling.py); no retrieval database ships with it. Nothing downloaded.

scope.note: Benchmark, not a model: 88 PDB-derived protein-peptide complexes (linear peptides 6-18 residues; macrocycles with a ring of at least 12 atoms and 1-20 residues; entries released after 2023-06-01, resolution <3 A, deduplicated, manually QC'd, prepared with Schrodinger Protein Preparation Workflow) plus evaluation code. Routes to modality 'benchmark'; consistent with displayed structure-prediction benchmarks FoldBench, PXMeter and KinConfBench (KinConfBench is similarly narrow). Adversarial caveats, not exclusion grounds: small n (88), single task (bound peptide pose at a known receptor), released by the company whose own unreleased model it showcases, not peer reviewed, and the 2023-06-01 time split was set against Boltz-2's training data, so models trained on later PDB snapshots may have seen these entries. Catalog-consistency blind spot: the far more widely used PoseBusters benchmark is not in the catalog either.

identity.note: Paper and hub bundle are the same model. Evidence: (a) checkpoint configs match the paper's architecture exactly (12 encoder layers, 12 heads, d_model 768, self-distillation head 4096/2048/256); (b) the scRep_20260717_3M manifest lists 57 shards summing to 2,803,535 cells, exactly the paper's scRep-3M corpus (1,136,218 Tabula Sapiens + 1,667,317 CELLxGENE); (c) the scRep_20260625_30M manifest lists 833 CELLxGENE files summing to 59,835,009 cells under a path named cellxgene_251108_thre1k3k, matching the paper's 59.8M-profile pool (>1,000 genes, >3,000 counts) from which 30.72M profiles were sampled; (d) checkpoint names match the paper's scRep-3M / scRep-30M. Author provenance: HF uploader jlu-wsj has display name 'wangshengjie' (first and corresponding author Shengjie Wang, School of AI, Jilin University per Crossref), no orgs, one model; all 5 commits by jlu-wsj on 2026-09-01; manifest paths contain 'liqiuyi' (last author Qiuyi Li). Checkpoints were not public anywhere else, so a third-party re-upload is implausible. LIMIT: no explicit link in either direction. The preprint's Code availability says code and checkpoints 'will be released' on publication and does not cite the hub; the card does not cite the paper or name authors. Distinguished from the HybriDNA hold precedent (uploader-asserted, card/variant and org mismatch): here every content check matches. Not a duplicate: no scRep / jlu-wsj / 747784 match in the baseline, models_final.json or the hold register. Name collisions exist (SCREP 2024 drug-response predictor; screp R enrichment-plot package) and are unrelated.

scope.note: Pretrained self-supervised scRNA-seq encoder (teacher-student latent self-distillation, cell- and gene-token objectives, no reconstruction loss) used frozen across several downstream analyses: clustering/annotation (KNN label transfer, group-disjoint folds), marker-gene prioritisation, TF-associated gene programs, trajectory/pseudotime. Broader than one task; modality singlecell is correct.

artifact.note: HF API: gated=false, private=false, 32 files. identity.note: Paper, repository and checkpoint point at one another. The bioRxiv preprint (10.64898/2026.08.25.746866, v1 posted 2026-08-28; corresponding author Bin Chen, Michigan State University) names github.com/Bin-Chen-Lab/insilicoCell as the location of 'user documentation, model weights and the code'. The repository README cites that DOI and links the checkpoint archive on the chenlab-data-public S3 bucket and the binchenlab/InsilicoCell Hugging Face dataset. The repository is not a fork. Nothing in the baseline identity table matches (searched for normalized 'insilicocell', 'insilico', 'Bin-Chen-Lab', 'octad', drug/perturb/screen names). The closest baseline records are PerturbGen and ScreenShot (held), which are different models from different labs. Not a duplicate and not a rename.

scope.note: In scope, with limits the record should state. It is a supervised multi-modal, multi-task transformer pretrained on more than 88 million labelled samples across seven tasks: drug sensitivity, drug-induced expression, drug-protein binding, TF-gene association, gene effect, mutation and CNV. It generalizes to unseen cells, compounds and proteins, so it is broader than one task. Adversarial points: (a) the released checkpoints are seven stage-2 task-specialized TorchScript modules plus a cell-embedding encoder; the stage-1 shared multi-task model is not released separately; (b) the model architecture is shipped only as TorchScript, and training and fine-tuning code are promised after acceptance, so out-of-the-box reuse is inference on the seven tasks plus cell embeddings; (c) the cell-context encoder is an autoencoder trained on about 1,144 DepMap cell lines, so single-cell, spatial and patient uses are author-reported adaptations. None of these makes it a single-task predictor or a thin fine-tune. Modality 'multimodal' is correct: bulk cell-line transcriptomes plus SMILES, gene and protein inputs.

artifact.note: The checkpoint archive is public and needs no login. HEAD returned 200 with Content-Length 1,375,041,807, Content-Type application/zip and Last-Modified 2026-04-24. A 64 KB tail range request (HTTP 206) read the zip central directory without downloading any weights. It lists 11 entries: seven task checkpoints of about 186 MB each (drug_response, drug-induced_gene_exp_change, drug-protein_binding_affinity, TF-gene_association, gene_effect_score, gene_mutation_status, CNV), plus cell_embedding.pt (about 80 MB), gene_embedding.csv and a ProtT5 UniProt embedding cache. The archive contains no licence file. The demo scripts load these files with torch.jit.load. The Hugging Face dataset is public and ungated and holds 14 benchmark test-set CSVs (sample-level and entity-level holdout for each of the seven tasks); the training splits are not released. The hosted MCP endpoint responds (HTTP 406 to a plain GET, as expected without MCP headers). I did not connect to it or use it.

terms.note: The proposal is roughly correct but its status wording is incomplete. Code: Apache-2.0 per the GitHub licence API and the LICENSE file (added 2026-06-18, copyright placeholder left unfilled). That licence covers the inference scripts; the model architecture is distributed only inside the TorchScript checkpoints. Weights: the S3 archive states no licence, and its file listing shows no licence file, so it should be worded as no licence stated (all rights reserved by default), not merely 'without a separately stated weight licence'. Benchmark test sets: Apache-2.0 according to the Hugging Face dataset card. They derive from third-party sources (LINCS, BindingDB, ChEA, CTRP, DepMap) whose own terms I did not check. Hosted MCP server: free access; the README states limits (10 h per job, 5,000-row inline requests, 1 GB uploads, 8 h result retention) but no terms of use. The CC BY-NC 4.0 licence applies to the preprint text only. I found no NC terms on code, weights, data or server, so noncommercial=false holds, but it is not evidence of a permissive weight licence.

urls.note: All three proposed URLs resolve and show what their labels claim. https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.25.746866 returns 302 to biorxiv.org, ending at https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.08.25.746866v1 with HTTP 200. https://github.com/Bin-Chen-Lab/insilicoCell returns 200 (API 200, Apache-2.0, last push 2026-10-07). The S3 checkpoint archive returns 200 to HEAD. Caveat: this code_link points directly at a 1.4 GB zip, so any link audit should use HEAD. scMulan already has a direct-download link, so there is precedent. Suggested addition: the official Hugging Face benchmark dataset (page 200, API 200).

text.note: No inflated claims and year 2026 is correct, but 'io' and 'description' cover only three of the seven tasks. They omit gene-name inputs, dose and time, and the TF-gene, gene effect, mutation and CNV outputs. 'Hosted server for large screening jobs' is partly misleading: the README recommends the local terminal route for large-scale inference and caps hosted jobs at 10 h. The audit_note should also say that the released checkpoints are task-specialized, that architecture code is TorchScript-only, and that training splits and fine-tuning code are pending acceptance.

identity.note: Paper (arXiv 2608.17872, Kaspar, Ignatov, Boeva; ETH Zurich per model cards), repository RamonKaspar/DistillPath (self-described 'Official implementation', not a fork, README links paper and hub collection) and hub owner RamonK (full name 'Ramon Kaspar', first author) are the same model family; the arXiv abstract itself links the GitHub repo and the RamonK hub collection. Not a duplicate or rename of any baseline record: baseline holds the teachers (UNI/UNI2-h, Virchow/Virchow2, H-optimus-0/1) and kaiko's Midnight, but no DistillPath, kaiko ViT-S/16 or H0-mini record. Hub search for 'DistillPath' returns only the six RamonK repos (no third-party re-uploads).

scope.note: Pretrained, task-agnostic 22M ViT-S/16 pathology tile encoders evaluated on 8 EVA tile classification/segmentation datasets (seven-task mean reported), 9 HEST gene-expression tasks and PLISM robustness; reusable via timm. Modality spatial is correct. In scope by precedent (GigaPath-Flash, a displayed distilled compact pathology encoder). Adversarial note: this is a 50,000-step distillation of an existing encoder (kaiko ViT-S/16) by a third party, closer to a derivative than a new foundation model, but it is not a single-task fine-tune.

artifact.note: Six public, ungated (gated:false) checkpoints on Hugging Face, each listing model.safetensors, config.json, LICENSE and README: DistillPath-KS16-{UNI2h,HOpt0,Virchow2} (kaiko-initialised) and DistillPath-IS16-{UNI2h,HOpt0,Virchow2} (ImageNet-21k-initialised). The proposal inspected only two. The paper and README describe eight runs including KS16-H0mini (best HEST and PLISM student per the paper) and IS16-H0mini; no H0-mini-distilled checkpoint was found on the hub (author listing and DistillPath search) - 'not found' describes my search. No GitHub releases (0). Weights not downloaded.

terms.note: Code: MIT (GitHub licence API, LICENSE file). Weights: KS16 variants cardData license 'other', license_name 'kaiko-non-commercial-public-license' with the Kaiko Non-Commercial Public License v1 text in LICENSE (permits sharing Adapted Material for Non-Commercial purposes only); IS16-UNI2h and IS16-Virchow2 CC-BY-NC-4.0; IS16-HOpt0 Apache-2.0 (card: fully permissive incl. commercial; teacher H-optimus-0 is Apache-2.0). All ungated. Training data: public TCGA slides with a download script. Correction to proposal: the cards DO restate teacher terms (UNI2-h and Virchow2 CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) and assert the students contain no teacher weights. The teachers' own hub gating text defines derivatives to 'include models trained on outputs from' the model and bars their commercial use without prior approval, so four of six checkpoints carry teacher-side NC constraints in addition to their own licence; whether CC BY-NC-ND/no-redistribution terms permit publishing such students at all is a contested legal question I cannot settle. noncommercial=true is correct (any NC artifact), but status must not imply all weights are kaiko-NC.

urls.note: All proposed URLs resolve 200 and show what they claim (arXiv abs, GitHub repo, two hub model pages). Label 'Hugging Face (UNI2-h teacher)' / '(H-optimus-0 teacher)' is misleading: the links are DistillPath student checkpoints, not the teacher models; relabelled. Proposal source excerpt for README line 15 is correct. Added the hub collection (README-linked, 200) and the EVA-best KS16-Virchow2 checkpoint.

text.note: Corrections: (1) description said all encoders are initialised from kaiko ViT-S/16; three released checkpoints are ImageNet-21k-initialised (IS16). (2) 'aiming to approach their downstream performance' is vague; the paper's measured claim is the best variant within 0.015 of Virchow2 on the seven-task EVA mean, while no student reaches its teacher on HEST. (3) use_cases 'linear probing and multiple-instance learning' are not stated in the paper (no MIL, no slide-level experiments); replaced with what was evaluated. (4) io refined to 224x224 tiles -> 384-dim class and patch tokens. (5) claims.artifact_and_terms 'Teacher-model terms are not restated by the authors' is false. Year 2026 correct (v1 2026-08-18; ECCV 2026 MedFM-Bench workshop acceptance per arXiv comment).

identity.note: arXiv 2608.16718v1 (Yao, Li, Yu, Huang; UPenn; only version, 2026-08-17) names https://github.com/zhihuanglab/CytoFormer and https://huggingface.co/zhihuanglab/CytoFormer in its Code Availability section; the README links the hub repo and the hub card links the GitHub repo. Both sit under the Zhi Huang Group organisation, so they are the authors' own release, not a re-upload. Name searches on arXiv, Hugging Face and GitHub each return only this model. One Europe PMC hit (PMID 42268916, PLoS One 2026, cervical cytology classification) does not use the name in its abstract and is a different work. Not a duplicate or rename of a baseline record. It is a derivative of the baseline record bfm-uni-uni2-h: the encoder is UNI2-h fine-tuned end-to-end. The proposed description leaves this out.

scope.note: Borderline but in scope, with honest wording. Against: training is one supervised objective (cell-type classification: 16 per-organ linear heads, 103 outputs, 23 global types), fine-tuned from an existing catalog FM for 5 epochs; every transfer evaluation is still cell classification (PanNuke, CoNSeP, MoNuSAC, PUMA, active-learning epithelium detection); the hub pipeline_tag is image-classification. For: this is not a thin fine-tune (15.4M cells, full end-to-end update of a ViT-giant, a new molecular supervision source); the README documents extract_features() as a reusable 1536-d cell embedding; the authors report frozen-encoder transfer to organs and cell types outside training. The catalog already includes comparable supervised or fine-tuned encoders (SEAL, Cell Painting CNN/DeepProfiler). Modality spatial is correct (pathology).

artifact.note: Hub API: gated=auto, public repo with siblings checkpoint.pth (2,726,343,169 bytes, LFS), organ_celltype_map.json and README.md; created 2026-08-09. The weights file appears in the listing only; it was not downloaded and the gate was not passed. The card README returns 401 without login. GitHub holds the model definition, inference and cropping scripts and a viewer: there is no training code and there are no GitHub releases. The training labels/dataset were not found released (the paper builds them from public 10x Genomics Xenium data and HEST-1k). The README says the checkpoint holds the whole network, so UNI2-h weights are not needed for inference.

terms.note: CytoFormer's own terms are confirmed. Code: Penn Academic Software License (clause 4: internal research or non-commercial use only; no distribution or transfer without Penn's prior written permission). GitHub reports Other/NOASSERTION. Weights: card licence cc-by-nc-4.0, automatic contact-sharing gate, and no extra gated prompt in cardData. noncommercial=true is correct. Material caveat missing from the proposal: the checkpoint is a fine-tune of UNI2-h, whose hub terms are CC-BY-NC-ND 4.0, prohibit commercial use of derivatives, and require users to agree 'not to distribute, publish or reproduce a copy of the model'. The CC BY-NC 4.0 label on CytoFormer, which allows adaptation and sharing, therefore conflicts with the upstream terms. I found no statement of upstream permission in the paper, README or visible card. Status wording must name this. If the orchestrator treats an unresolved upstream licence conflict as unclear terms, HOLD is the fallback.

urls.note: All proposed URLs resolve with HTTP 200 and show what their labels say: arXiv abs (2608.16718), GitHub repo, and the Hugging Face model page (gated, licence cc-by-nc-4.0). The proposal's raw LICENSE URL (200) and hub API URL (200) also check out. The 'Hugging Face (gated)' label is accurate.

text.note: Facts in the proposal are accurate: 15,422,352 cells, 81 sections (54 from the 10x portal, 27 from HEST-1k), 16 organs, 23 cell types (counted from the README organ table), year 2026. Corrections: (1) the description must say the encoder is UNI2-h fine-tuned end-to-end, so readers see it is a derivative of a catalog record; (2) the io should include the organ identifier input, the 56 µm field of view, organ-restricted output and the 1536-d embedding; (3) the status should say 'inference code' (no training code) and name the upstream UNI2-h terms; (4) the audit_note should record that the full text was read (the proposal used the abstract only) and that transfer is author-reported and limited to cell-classification benchmarks.

identity.note: Paper (Nat Biotechnol, DOI 10.1038/s41587-025-02663-3; authors R. Bushuiev ... T. Pluskal), repository pluskal-lab/DreaMS, Zenodo 10997887 (creator Roman Bushuiev, IOCB Prague) and Hugging Face roman-bushuiev/DreaMS are the same model and author-run: the paper cites the GitHub repo (ref 110) and Zenodo weights (ref 105); the README badges link both hubs; the code's download_pretrained_model() pulls from roman-bushuiev/DreaMS. Hub checkpoints embedding_model.ckpt and ssl_model.ckpt have byte sizes identical to the Zenodo files. Not a third-party re-upload. No duplicate in the 444-row baseline or under-review register (searched dreams, pluskal, bushuiev, spectr, MS/MS, metabolom; the only substring hit is FoldFlow-2's DreamFold GitHub org, unrelated).

scope.note: Pretrained (self-supervised masked m/z + retention-order objectives, 116M parameters) and reusable: zero-shot embeddings via dreams_embeddings() plus fine-tuning to spectral similarity, molecular fingerprints, chemical properties and fluorine detection. The paper itself frames it as able to 'act as a foundation model for MS/MS'. Broader than one task. Modality 'molecule' fits (small-molecule MS/MS; no mass-spec modality exists).

artifact.note: Zenodo 10997887 open, v1, is_latest, files embedding_model.ckpt (1,241,290,418 B) and ssl_model.ckpt (1,392,710,212 B).
