identity.note: Paper (DOI 10.1016/j.media.2022.102559, Medical Image Analysis vol. 81, Oct 2022, PMID 35952419; Wang X, Yang S, ... Han X) states code and pretrained model at github.com/Xiyue-Wang/TransPath; repo README links the same Elsevier PII S1361841522002043 that the DOI resolves to and links the ctranspath.pth Drive file. Author-owned repo, not a fork. No normalized-name, alias or URL match in the 445-row baseline (no 'ctranspath'/'transpath'/repo/DOI/Drive-ID hit) and no prior mention anywhere in Foundation_models/. Correction: the proposed alias 'TransPath' is wrong. TransPath is the separate MICCAI 2021 predecessor model with its own checkpoint in the same repo. Listing it as an alias would conflate two models in future identity matching, so it should be removed. All Hugging Face copies found (jamesdolezal/CTransPath, kaczmarj/CTransPath, 1aurent/swin_tiny_patch4_window7_224.CTransPath and others) are third-party re-uploads, not the official artifact.

scope.note: This is a pretrained, reusable self-supervised tile encoder (CNN stem + Swin-T backbone, SRCL pretraining on unlabelled TCGA+PAIP patches, about 15 million per the README). The paper evaluates five downstream task types on nine public datasets, so it is broader than one task. The README recommends it as the preferred histopathology feature extractor. Modality 'spatial' is correct under the MAINTENANCE.md rule that pathology routes to spatial.

artifact.note: The official README links the weights to Google Drive file 1DoDx_70_TLj98gTf6YTXnu4tFhsFocDX. Its public view page returned HTTP 200 without sign-in, with title 'ctranspath.pth' and isItemTrashed false. Weights were not downloaded. The model also needs a modified timm 0.5.4 build, which is a separate public Drive file titled 'timm-0.5.4.tar' (HTTP 200). The repo has no GitHub releases and no official Hugging Face card. Limits: the weights sit on a personal Drive, which is a link-rot risk, and there is no checksum.

terms.note: The proposal missed a non-commercial statement. LICENSE.md is unmodified GPL-3.0 (GitHub licence API: GPL-3.0), but the README License section says 'TransPath is released under the GPLv3 License and is available for non-commercial academic purposes.' That statement covers the repository's released code and models. Under the catalog rule (noncommercial=true if ANY artifact or access route has NC terms), noncommercial must be true; the proposed false is wrong. The two terms conflict: GPL-3.0 forbids further restrictions, while the README adds an NC restriction. No separate weight licence exists. The weights are ungated. Status wording must state the NC statement and the conflict.

urls.note: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.media.2022.102559 returned 302 to linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S1361841522002043 (200), and Crossref shows the matching title and journal. https://github.com/Xiyue-Wang/TransPath returned 200 and is the official repo. The Drive weights URL returned 200 with the page titled ctranspath.pth. All labels match their content. Note that the Elsevier article is paywalled; only the abstract was checked, via Europe PMC.

text.note: Three text fixes are needed. (1) 'widely used as a frozen tile feature extractor' is a popularity claim not supported by the primary sources; it is replaced with the authors' stated recommendation. (2) use_cases lists 'survival models', which the paper does not evaluate; it is replaced with the paper's evaluated tasks: patch retrieval, patch classification, weakly supervised WSI classification, mitosis detection and gland segmentation. (3) 'about 15 million patches' is supported only by the README ('about 15,000,000 images'); the abstract says only 'massively unlabeled'. The 768-d output in the proposal's claims is consistent with timm swin_tiny with the head removed, but the repo does not state it, so the io field omits the dimension. Year 2022 is correct (online 2022-07-30, issue Oct 2022). The description wording 'hybrid CNN-Swin' matches the abstract.

One pocket-conditioned pretrained model covers de novo design, fragment growing, fragment linking, docking, partial docking, programmable design and synthesizable design in virtual chemical spaces (README feature list; abstract lists constrained and unconstrained docking, fragment linking and growing, de novo design). Training is a masking-based multi-task framework over a curated 836,259-point protein-ligand dataset assembled from CrossDocked, BindingNet v2 and BigBind, and two reusable checkpoints are released, so the record is a pretrained reusable artifact, not a method without weights. Modality 'molecule' confirmed: the model generates ligands/poses conditioned on a pocket, exactly the precedent set by bfm-pocketxmol (molecule). 'complex' is a defensible alternative but would break that precedent; keep molecule.

artifact.note: Weights exist as claimed, verified from metadata only (no download). Zenodo record 22754501 file listing returns 8 files including lddm.ckpt (168265378 bytes, md5 7f11f7a15bbdf84b1a08a60fd3ad9f2f) and lddm_CDBB.ckpt (168461579 bytes, md5 f79225b6b71af5d042a06265e666afdf), plus ligands.sdf geometry reference and five SynSpace chemical-space files; the Zenodo HTML page lists the same 8 filenames. Code is public and active (MIT LICENSE.md, pushed 2026-10-10, pinned uv.lock, Docker image referenced in README). No official Hugging Face artifact exists and none is claimed: a hub search for 'lddm' returns only two unrelated repositories (LDD/MLM, lddmm1/libero10_task9_smoke). No hosted API or server was found, and the proposal correctly claims none.

terms.note: Component-specific terms confirmed and noncommercial=true is correct. Code: MIT, LICENSE.md, 'Copyright (c) 2026 Ilia Igashov, Arne Schneuing, Adrian Dobbelstein' (GitHub licence API reports spdx_id MIT). Weights: README licence table and the Zenodo description agree that lddm.ckpt (CD+BB+BN, the paper model) is CC-BY-NC 4.0 because it was partially trained on BindingNet, while lddm_CDBB.ckpt (CD+BB) is MIT. The Zenodo record-level machine-readable licence field is mit-license, with the NC carve-out stated only in prose, so the catalog must keep the per-checkpoint wording rather than inherit 'MIT' from the record field. Synthesizable design: Enamine REAL reactions and building blocks are not redistributed and need a licence requested from Enamine; the repository ships a smaller SynSpace-derived space of 44,944 building blocks, which the Zenodo description curates from Mcule's supplier catalog of 5 December 2022 and asserts under MIT along with all non-lddm.ckpt files. Because the paper checkpoint route is NC, noncommercial=true. Status wording corrected to name the access routes explicitly (MIT code, Zenodo weights, no hosted API) in line with MAINTENANCE.md access-wording rule.

urls.note: All proposed URLs resolve and show what their labels say, but two need changing before release. (1) The proposal cites https://zenodo.org/api/records/22754501 inside proposed_record.sources; the catalog never puts an API endpoint in a record (only api.boltz.bio appears, as a product URL) and cites Zenodo as https://zenodo.org/records/NNN or https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.NNN. Replaced with https://zenodo.org/records/22754501, whose content I verified (title, 8 filenames, licence prose). (2) Following the bfm-pocketxmol precedent the Zenodo record belongs in code_links, not only in sources; added. Reachability note for the link audit: zenodo.org/records/22754501 and doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22754501 both return 403 to a plain curl (Zenodo bot protection), while the Zenodo API returns 200 and a normal browser fetch of the record page succeeds; existing catalog records use the same two URL forms, so this is a known audit quirk, not a dead link. Paper, repo and all evidence URLs returned 200.

text.note: Description, io, use_cases and year are factual with no inflated claims (year 2026 matches the 2026-09-18 posting and the 2026-09-14 Zenodo publication date; the record does not repeat the preprint's experimental-success claims). Two text-level defects, both fixed in corrected_record: the proposed record omits six schema-required fields (id, date_added, canonical, verified, audit_priority, audit_source), so it would fail validate_catalog.py as submitted; and status needed the explicit access-route distinction. identity.note: arXiv 2602.22251 (v4, 2026-05-13; ICLR 2026 FM4Science) names github.com/Zatom-AI/zatom as the code/weights location. The GitHub repo (Zatom-AI org, not a fork, created 2025-08-14, pushed 2026-07-25) describes itself as the official Zatom-1 repository and cites the arXiv paper. The HF model card links back to that repo and cites the paper; the HF Zatom-AI org members are Alex Morehead (first author) and Ty Perez (author Tynan Perez), so the HF upload is author-made. The Zenodo record (creator Morehead, Alex) is the download location the GitHub README actually uses. No Zatom/Platom name, alias or URL match in fm_identity.tsv (445 rows), records_under_review.json or the 2026-10-10 evidence folder. The successor Zatom-2 is a separate held candidate.

scope.note: Pretrained and reusable, and broader than one task: unconditional 3D molecule and crystal generation plus finetuned multi-task property, energy and force prediction from the shared trunk. Modality 'molecule' fits catalog precedent (Uni-Mol2, UMA, SMI-TED, Suiren-1.0). Borderline, and left to the curator: this is a chemistry/materials model, not a biology-specific one. Its link to biology runs through small and drug-like molecules (QM9, GEOM-Drugs) and an OMol25 (4M) checkpoint that the paper says includes biomolecules. The pretraining scale is modest: the baseline joint model uses QM9 (~130k molecules) plus MP20 (45,231 crystals), at 80M/160M/300M parameters. GEOM-Drugs, QMOF and OMol25 are separate pretraining checkpoints. The paper's own title says 'Towards a ... Foundation Model'.

artifact.note: HF Zatom-AI/Zatom-1: gated=false, private=false, 26 .ckpt files stored as LFS (0.44-4.7 GB) plus README and figure. Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.19766997 (v1.0.2, open, published 2026-05-13): 26 .ckpt files plus generated samples and LeMat-GenBench result zips. The two checkpoint sets differ by one file each. The README's wget commands point to Zenodo; it does not link the HF model repo. Correction: the proposal says '~27 checkpoints'; the actual count is 26 on each host. Weights were not downloaded or executed.

terms.note: Code: the GitHub LICENSE is the LBNL modified 3-clause BSD with an Enhancements clause and a DOE government-rights notice; GitHub reports 'Other'/NOASSERTION. The paper says Zatom-1 is 'available under a permissive BSD license'. HF weights: the card's YAML says license: mit, and the HF repo has no LICENSE file. Zenodo weights record: cc-by-4.0, open access. All three declarations are permissive and none is non-commercial, so noncommercial=false is correct. The labels disagree across distributions, and the record should say so. Datasets are re-hosted under the Zatom-AI HF org; per the paper, the source datasets carry their own licences (e.g. QM9 CC-BY-4.0, MP20 MIT). No hosted API or server.

urls.note: All proposed URLs returned HTTP 200 and show what their labels claim: arxiv.org/abs/2602.22251, github.com/Zatom-AI/zatom, huggingface.co/Zatom-AI/Zatom-1, zenodo.org/api/records/19766997. text.note: Description is accurate but omits scale and pretraining data; the corrected record adds both (80M-300M; QM9 + MP20 baseline joint pretraining; separate GEOM-Drugs, QMOF and OMol25 checkpoints). The io string implied that generation takes atom types and coordinates as input; generation samples from noise. identity.note: Both arXiv preprints (2606.02419v4 DPA4, 2608.19041v2 DPA4C) share authors Li T., Xue J., Zhang L., Zhang D., Wang H. (DeePMD-kit maintainers). Both papers' availability statements point to deepmodeling/deepmd-kit from v3.2.0; v3.2.0 (published 2026-08-19, not prerelease) release notes introduce the DPA4 family. HF org deepmodelingcommunity is referenced by the official deepmd/pretrained/registry.py (DPA4-OMat24, DPA3-Omol-Large); the two OMol repos are not themselves in the registry but sit in the same org, carry arXiv tags 2606.02419 / 2608.19041 and link to docs.deepmodeling.com. Official docs state DPA4 is the DeePMD-kit implementation of the SeZM architecture, so 'SeZM' should be added as an alias. No DPA/DeePMD/SeZM name, alias or URL in the baseline identity file; no other discovery lane proposes it. Not a duplicate of UMA (bfm-uma) or FeNNix-Bio1.

scope.note: Pretrained universal MLIPs with released checkpoints and documented fine-tuning; same class as displayed precedents UMA (bfm-uma) and FeNNix-Bio1, modality 'molecule' consistent. Caveats against the biological remit: the family is materials-first (DPA4 headline benchmark is Matbench Discovery; DPA4C benchmarks are OMat24, MatPES, diamond carbon, FCC copper). Biological relevance rests only on the OMol25-trained checkpoints (OMol25 spans biomolecules, metal complexes, electrolytes). DPA4C-OMol is a weak molecular model: OMol25 OOD energy MAE 16.77-40.97 kcal/mol vs 0.92-8.02 for DPA4; the DPA4C paper itself says the accuracy gap 'widens substantially' on molecules. Acceptable as one family record only if the description states this.

artifact.note: HF API: DPA4-OMol and DPA4C-OMol both gated=false, private=false, created 2026-08-20; each lists five .pt checkpoints (Air, Mini, Nano, Neo, Plus; OMol25-100M-v20260820) plus training-config .json and README. DPA4-Pro (best OMol25 result in paper/card) is NOT released. Org listing also shows DPA4-OMat24, DPA4C-OMat (CC BY-NC 4.0) and DPA4-Beta; no MatPES-trained checkpoints on the hub, so the proposed description's claim that checkpoints are trained on 'OMat24, MatPES or OMol25' overstates released artifacts. Neither paper's availability statement mentions weights (code only). Weights not downloaded or executed.

identity.note: Paper, repo and hub artifact form one official chain. KERMT v1 preprint (arXiv 2510.12719) has Merck and NVIDIA BioNeMo authors and points to github.com/NVIDIA-Digital-Bio/KERMT, which now redirects to NVIDIA-BioNeMo/KERMT (not a fork, Apache-2.0). The repo README and the v2.0.0 release notes name nvidia/NV-KERMT-70M-v2 and arXiv 2606.11508. The HF card (official nvidia org) links back to the repo and the v2.0.0 tag. Not a duplicate: the baseline has bfm-grover (Tencent GROVER) and no KERMT/NV-KERMT name, alias or URL. Lineage caveat: KERMT v1 shipped no weights of its own and was evaluated on the published GROVER base model (the README fine-tuning example uses grover_base.pt). On its own, v1 would be a GROVER reimplementation. A separate record is justified only by the independently pretrained v2.0 Contrastive KERMT checkpoint (new SMILES decoder and cMIM objective, vocabularies rebuilt). Contrastive KERMT/v2.0 is NVIDIA-only; Merck co-authored only v1.

scope.note: Self-supervised pretraining on about 11.1M molecules for 100 epochs. The card presents it as a fine-tunable backbone or feature extractor for multi-endpoint ADMET, broader than one task. Same class as the GROVER and KPGT records already in the catalog. Modality molecule is correct. Narrowness caveat: the v2 preprint says its evaluation is restricted to ADME endpoints in three multi-task datasets. On-target potency was evaluated only for KERMT v1, which used GROVER weights.

artifact.note: HF API: nvidia/NV-KERMT-70M-v2, gated=false, private=false, created 2026-06-08. File listing: kermt_contrastive_v2.0.pt (282,379,314 bytes, LFS), pretrain_atom_vocab.json, pretrain_bond_vocab.json, pretrain_smiles_vocab.pkl, LICENSE, model-card subcards. Weights were not downloaded or executed. The v2.0.0 GitHub release has no assets: weights are linked from HF and NGC. The NGC route was not verified (NGC API 401 unauthenticated; the catalog page redirect ended in 404 for curl). The HF API reports 0 downloads, a weak uptake signal and not a defect. The name '70M' matches the 70.61M pretraining parameters (preprint Table). The downstream encoder is 56.95M after the decoder and contrastive heads are discarded.

terms.note: Code: Apache-2.0 (GitHub licence API, LICENSE file; third_party.txt lists Apache-2.0 cuik-molmaker). Weights and vocab files: NVIDIA Open Model License (HF cardData license_name nvidia-open-model-license; the HF LICENSE file is the Agreement, last modified 2025-10-24). It states 'Models are commercially usable' and allows derivative models. Conditions: redistribution needs a 'Licensed by NVIDIA Corporation under the NVIDIA Open Model License' notice. Rights terminate on guardrail circumvention or on copyright/patent litigation. NVIDIA may update the Agreement. Ungated, with no click-through on HF. Data: KERMT v1 benchmark splits on Figshare (10.6084/m9.figshare.30350548.v2) are labelled GPL, with subsets under their original licences (e.g. CC-BY-SA). The v2 card's pretraining sources include ZINC15 (custom licence), ChEMBL (CC BY-SA 3.0) and ExpansionRX (HF dataset tag cc-by-4.0). No NC term found on any artifact, so noncommercial=false is correct. Status wording should name the OML conditions, not just 'commercial use permitted'.

urls.note: All four record URLs resolve (HTTP 200): arxiv.org/abs/2510.12719, arxiv.org/abs/2606.11508, github.com/NVIDIA-BioNeMo/KERMT, huggingface.co/nvidia/NV-KERMT-70M-v2. Each shows what its label says. Stale cross-reference: the HF card still says the Contrastive KERMT manuscript is 'in preparation; arXiv URL to be added', but the repo README and v2.0.0 release notes link arXiv 2606.11508. The v1 paper's code link uses the old org NVIDIA-Digital-Bio, which redirects correctly.

text.note: Corrections needed. (1) The description says v2.0 'adds contrastive and chemistry-specific self-supervised pretraining'. The atom/bond-context and functional-group self-supervision already existed in GROVER/KERMT. v2.0 adds a SMILES-reconstruction decoder and an in-batch contrastive (cMIM) objective (release notes: 'Keeps the v1 graph-transformer encoder + chemistry-specific vocabulary heads, and adds two new pretraining-only heads'). (2) 'Developed by Merck and NVIDIA' applies to KERMT v1 only; the card says Contrastive KERMT was developed by NVIDIA. (3) The description should state that v1 used the published GROVER weights, so the record's own weights are the 2026 v2.0 checkpoint. (4) io/use_cases list potency for the released checkpoint, but the v2 preprint evaluates ADME only; potency belongs to KERMT v1. (5) The audit note should flag that the released checkpoint's pretraining corpus includes unlabeled molecules from its own evaluation benchmarks (Biogen, ExpansionRX, ChEMBL-MT). The preprint calls these gains label-free/transductive, not strictly inductive. Year 2025 kept under the catalog's family convention (first-member year, e.g. RFdiffusion/RFD3 = 2023, Phikon/Phikon-v2 = 2023). The KERMT preprint is from 2025-10-14, but the first KERMT-specific weights date from 2026-06; the maintainer could reasonably choose 2026.

Csanyi). Both data-availability statements point to github.com/ACEsuit/mace-off/tree/main; ACEsuit/mace README links the same repo and ships a mace_off() calculator. Official author repo, not a fork or re-upload. No name, alias or URL match in the 444-row baseline (molecule MLIP neighbours UMA and FeNNix-Bio1 are different models); no prior MACE decision found in Foundation_models/evidence or records_under_review.json.

scope.note: Pretrained transferable force fields reused for inference or as a fine-tuning start (ACEsuit/mace README, 'Pretrained Foundation Models' section). Paper frames it for biomolecular simulation (peptide folding, solvated crambin). Inclusion rests on the catalog precedent of UMA and FeNNix-Bio1 (MLIPs in 'molecule'); modality 'molecule' consistent. Limits: 10 elements (H,C,N,O,F,P,S,Cl,Br,I), neutral closed-shell systems, short-range (no explicit long-range electrostatics).

artifact.note: GitHub contents API lists real binary files (not LFS pointers): mace_off23/MACE-OFF23_small.model (7.3 MB), _medium (18.4 MB), _large (55.5 MB), MACE-OFF23b_medium (18.4 MB), mace_off24/MACE-OFF24_medium.model (18.4 MB), plus train_scripts. MACE-OFF23b is not described in the paper, only in the release note.

identity.note: The JCTC paper (10.1021/acs.jctc.6c01169; Picha, Karwounopoulos, Erhard, Boresch, Heid; Crossref issued 2026-09-03, vol 22(18) 9274-9289) states in its Data Availability section that all GRACE-OFF models are in github.com/heid-lab/grace-off. That repository is owned by heid-lab (corresponding author Esther Heid), is not a fork, and its README says the GRACE-OFF models are in models/1l and models/2l. The b_off_{small,medium,large} directories match the paper's Table 1 hyperparameters (checked for 1L-M, 2L-M, 2L-L and 1L-S). Neither Hugging Face nor GitHub search found a third-party re-upload. No normalized name, alias or URL match in the baseline (445 rows). The closest records are FeNNix-Bio1, UMA and UBio-MolFM, which are different models. The repo also holds two a_wpS_{small,medium} variants that the paper does not describe. The README does not state which directory matches which paper model name; the mapping above is inferred from the hyperparameters.

scope.note: Transferable MLIP pretrained from scratch on SPICE v2.0 (Small-molecule/Protein Interaction Chemical Energies) and used for many downstream simulations: single points, torsion scans, liquid properties, water, and biomolecular MD. The paper calls it a 'foundation potential'. The catalog precedent is FeNNix-Bio1, a SPICE2-trained MLIP accepted in molecule on 2026-08-13. Modality molecule is correct. Limits to state: neutral molecules only, 10 elements (H, C, N, O, F, P, S, Cl, Br, I), charged species and reactions excluded by design ('charged species and reactive processes are both outside the scope', Introduction). The biomolecular evidence is only an MD stability test on gas-phase Ala15 and solvated crambin. Scope passes, but the record text must not overstate biomolecular coverage.

artifact.note: The git tree (451 blobs, not truncated) holds TensorFlow SavedModel, casted_model, final_model and checkpoint files with real sizes (for example 2l/a_wpS_medium final_model variables 7.2 MB; 1l/b_off_large saved_model variables 8.2 MB). They are ordinary git files, not LFS pointers. There are no tagged releases, so the access route is the main branch. The repo also redistributes third-party MACE-OFF23_small, MACE-OFF23_large and MACE-OFF24_medium .model files. Inference per the README is via tensorpotential.calculator.TPCalculator from ICAMS/grace-tensorpotential (latest release 0.6.1, 2026-09-03). Training, validation and test data are on Zenodo (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18662354, which resolves to record 18662355; open; CC BY 4.0; published 2026-03). GRACE-OFF is not in ICAMS's grace_models foundation-model registry (README and code search). No hosted API found. Not executed or downloaded.

terms.note: heid-lab/grace-off: the root LICENSE is MIT ('Copyright (c) 2026 heid-lab'), added 2026-04-03. It is the only licence file in the tree. The redistributed MACE-OFF model files are under the Academic Software Licence upstream (ACEsuit/mace-off LICENSE.md and README: 'free to use them for academic purpose, but not for commercial purposes'), and no ASL notice accompanies them in this repo. ICAMS/grace-tensorpotential (gracemaker/tensorpotential), which the documented inference route requires, is ASL: 'grant of rights under the License is for academic non-commercial use only' (LICENSE.md section 13a). Zenodo data: CC BY 4.0. Paper: CC BY 4.0. No gating. noncommercial=true is correct because the only documented runtime is ASL. The proposed status needs to name the data licence, the ungated access and the third-party ASL MACE-OFF files, and must not read as 'MIT covers everything in the repo'.

urls.note: https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.6c01169 redirects (302) to pubs.acs.org, which returns 403 (bot challenge) to scripted clients. The DOI is confirmed via Crossref (200), and the open full text is at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13602931/ (200; title, CC-BY 4.0 notice and repo link present), which should be added so the link audit has a 200 paper link. https://github.com/heid-lab/grace-off is 200 and contains the models. https://github.com/ICAMS/grace-tensorpotential is 200 ('GRACE models and gracemaker (as implemented in TensorPotential package)'). https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18662354 resolves to https://zenodo.org/records/18662355 (200 without a custom user agent; one curl run with a browser user agent got 403).

text.note: Description and io are accurate, but they omit the neutral-only, 10-element restriction. use_cases 'solvated biomolecule MD' goes beyond the evidence (a stability test on two systems). It is corrected to name Ala15 and crambin. The alias 'GRACE Organic Force Field' comes from the abstract ('introduce GRACE-OFF (GRACE Organic Force Field)'). Year 2026 is correct: ChemRxiv v1 posted 2026-04-02, v2 2026-08-18, JCTC 2026-09-03. The proposal's justification calls it 'in the August-September window', but v1 and the MIT-licensed model repo were public by early April 2026, before the 2026-08-13 baseline. This does not block inclusion; it is an earlier miss, not new work. Performance claims (2L beats MACE-OFF; faster than UMA S) are the authors' own benchmarks and are kept out of the record.

identity.note: Paper (arXiv 2610.08400v1, Petersen, Tirsgaard, Cornet, Jordahn, Schmidt; submitted 2026-10-06) abstract links github.com/khelverskovp/atom-jepa and the HTML full text links huggingface.co/atom-jepa/atom-jepa. Repo (non-fork, created 2026-10-05, homepage = arXiv abs) calls itself the 'Official implementation' and links the HF repo and PyPI. HF org 'atom-jepa' lists three paper authors as members (Kasper Helverskov Petersen, Mikkel Jordahn, Rasmus Tirsgaard). PyPI atom-jepa 0.3.0 points to the same repo and HF models. Not in models_final.json, records_under_review.json or the identity baseline; distinct from bfm-mol-jepa (Boehringer, SMILES multimodal, different authors/URLs) and bfm-uni-mol/bfm-uni-mol2 (Uni-Mol supplies only the pretraining set). Only one proposal in the discovery lanes (molecule).

scope.note: Pretrained, reusable SSL encoders (fine-tune or frozen features) evaluated on many tasks (TDC/Biogen/ExpansionRX/ChEMBL-MT ADMET, QM9, Matbench) -> broader than one task. Modality 'molecule' correct for the molecules encoder (drug-like Uni-Mol set, ADMET use). The crystals encoder is materials science, outside biology; acceptable under the UMA precedent (bfm-uma, molecule, spans materials) but it should not be the record's emphasis. HF card states these are representations, not property predictors.

artifact.note: HF API: gated=false, private=false; siblings molecules/model.safetensors and crystals/model.safetensors (+config.json each); tree API shows each safetensors LFS file 156,380,852 bytes, consistent with ~39.0M fp32 parameters stated on the card. Configs: EquiformerV3, 8 layers, 256 channels, lmax 2, 6 A cutoff. GitHub releases v0.2.0/v0.3.0 have no assets (weights are on HF only). Weights not downloaded or executed; loadability not tested.

terms.note: Code MIT (GitHub licence API + LICENSE file; PyPI license_expression MIT); vendored EquiformerV3 and fairchem code carry MIT licence files; upstream atomicarchitects/equiformer_v3 is MIT. Weights CC BY 4.0 (HF cardData.license and README 'License' section), ungated, no NC term found -> noncommercial=false correct. No hosted API/server. Pretraining data are third-party (Uni-Mol set, Alexandria) and not redistributed by the project; their own terms not checked here. Crossref has a NeurIPS 2025 proceedings version of the same title (DOI 10.52202/085713-5269; author list adds Michael Pieler).

scope.note: Reusable released weights, multi-task (18 task types, 375 subtasks in paper Table 1), so not a single-task predictor and not a thin fine-tune (multi-stage SFT plus GRPO over 640,730 problems). Limit: no domain pretraining ('post-trained for chemistry without additional domain pretraining', abstract). Catalog precedent admits post-trained LLMs (TxGemma: Gemma fine-tuned on TDC; BioReason-Pro: SFT+RL reasoning model) and ChemDFM in molecule. Modality 'molecule' matches ChemDFM. Narrow I/O (answers are always a molecule; the card says it cannot answer 'What is the pKa of ...').

artifact.note: HF API futurehouse/ether0: gated=false, private=false, 21 model-*-of-00021.safetensors shards (~94.3 GB total), tokenizer, config, chat template, LICENSE; base_model mistralai/Mistral-Small-24B-Instruct-2501; created 2025-06-04, last modified 2025-06-24. Not downloaded. The model card states the released weights are post-safety-training and differ from the preprint's benchmarked checkpoint. GitHub repo has no releases; README: 'This repo does not contain training code'. Dataset futurehouse/ether0-benchmark: 325-example test split only; no training-set dataset found under the futurehouse HF org.

terms.note: Weights: HF cardData license apache-2.0 plus Apache-2.0 LICENSE file ('Copyright 2025 FutureHouse'); card: 'open weights under an Apache 2.0 license'. Code: GitHub licence API Apache-2.0 (LICENSE). Benchmark data: cardData cc-by-4.0 plus CC BY 4.0 LICENSE file. Base model Mistral-Small-24B-Instruct-2501: apache-2.0, ungated. No gating, no NC terms found, so noncommercial=false is correct. Status corrected: the proposed 'Open code + weights' overstated the code, which holds reward functions and data utilities with no training code.

urls.note: All three record URLs return 200 with matching titles: arxiv.org/abs/2506.17238 ('Training a Scientific Reasoning Model for Chemistry'), github.com/Future-House/ether0 ('A scientific reasoning model, dataset, and reward functions for chemistry'), huggingface.co/futurehouse/ether0 ('futurehouse/ether0 · Hugging Face').

text.note: Description said SFT and RL were both 'on 640,730 ... problems'. The paper and model card place RL on the 640,730 problems and SFT on reasoning traces (14,021 R1-derived traces initially, then filtered specialist traces). Corrected. '375 tasks' is the abstract's wording, but the body says '18 different tasks', with 375 as the Table 1 subtask total; reframed as 18 task types/375 subtasks. 'Experimentally grounded' is the authors' claim and was dropped from the description, because some rewards use ML verifiers (Molecular Transformer, a solubility model). Use cases were aligned to the model card task list, adding the not-a-property-predictor limit. io and year (2025) are supported.

identity.note: arXiv 2608.16419v3 'Data and Code Availability' names github.com/shapsider/PertMind (code/docs) and huggingface.co/tzcfly/PertMind (weights); v1 comments linked the same two; project page shapsider.github.io/PertMind links both. HF account tzcfly has fullname 'Zhenchao Tang' (first, equal-contribution author); HF repo and GitHub repo created within one second on 2026-08-17. Only one PertMind repo on HF; featherless.ai/friendli.ai listings seen in search are third-party serving, not official. No baseline match (no 'pertmind' normalized name/alias/URL; nearest PerturbGen and PertEval-scFM are different models). Provenance flag: v2 (22 Aug 2026) withdrawn with comment that co-authors did not consent to posting and 'No replacement version will be submitted'; v3 (6 Oct 2026) then submitted by a different author (Yaokun Li vs Zhenchao Tang) with 19 authors instead of 11 (all 11 original authors still listed). v3 re-endorses the same artifacts, so model identity is clear, but the dispute history must be in the audit note.

scope.note: Released checkpoint usable zero-shot; paper evaluates forward drug-response calls in held-out cell lines, reverse perturbation-condition ranking on CRISPRa/i (Schmidt) and Norman double perturbations, AssayBench screen prioritisation, GeneAgent process naming, and gene/cell/donor representations -> broader than one task by use, consistent with displayed precedents TxGemma and BioReason-Pro (multimodal). Limits a curator should see: training is a LoRA (rank 64) SFT+GRPO post-train of general Qwen3-4B-Base on ONE task (Up/Down/No for cell line x small molecule x gene from Tahoe-100M); no biology-specific pretraining; screen prioritisation and process naming use PertMind briefs to augment other LLMs (GPT-5.4, Gemini 3 Pro, Qwen3.5, GPT-4/GeneAgent); representation results encode PertMind text with OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 plus task-specific projections. Not a thin task-specific fine-tune in the catalog sense, but borderline; modality multimodal acceptable by precedent (text-only interface).

artifact.note: HF API: gated=false, private=false, sha 14a19cc, created and last modified 2026-08-17; siblings include model.safetensors (8,044,982,080 bytes, ~7.5 GiB bf16), config, tokenizer.json, chat_template.jinja, LICENSE, requirements.txt, inference_vllm.py, inference_transformers.py, tui_chat.py. GitHub tree: LICENSE, README.md, assets/Figure1.png, docs/ (project page) only; 2 commits on 2026-08-17; no releases. The paper's v3 statement 'Source code and usage documentation are available at' GitHub is overstated: no source or training code is there. Training corpus/trusted trajectories not released; source atlas Tahoe-100M is public. Weights not downloaded or run.

GitHub: Apache-2.0 (authenticated gh api repos/shapsider/PertMind/license -> spdx Apache-2.0; unauthenticated api.github.com call returned 403 rate-limit). Base model Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Base cardData license apache-2.0, ungated. No NC terms found on any artifact -> noncommercial=false correct. Card says 'released for research use, hypothesis generation, and method development' and lists clinical use as out of scope; these are non-binding statements, not licence terms. No hosted API. The paper's embedding pipeline depends on the proprietary OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 API, which is not part of the release. Tahoe-100M data terms not checked.

Description says 'perturbation atlases' (plural); training used one atlas (Tahoe-100M). use_cases omit that screen prioritisation/process naming work as briefs feeding other LLMs and that representations need an external OpenAI embedding model plus trained projections. Status should note the paper overstates GitHub code availability. audit_note should give the v2 withdrawal reason and author-list change, and LoRA single-task post-training. Year 2026 correct.

identity.note: arXiv 2501.08187 (v1 2025-01-14, v2 2025-01-15; Fang, Deng, Liu, Zhang, Qian, Yang, Fan, Chen) names the code repo and both hub checkpoints in its arXiv comment field (lower-case 'Instructcell' variants; huggingface.co/zjunlp/Instructcell-chat redirects to the canonical InstructCell-chat). GitHub zjunlp/InstructCell is not a fork, carries the paper title as description and links both zjunlp HF checkpoints; both hub cards carry the identical citation and the tag arxiv:2501.08187, and config.json declares architectures ['InstructCell']. Same owner org (zjunlp) for paper links, repo and hub, so endorsement is bidirectional; no third-party re-upload selected. No 'instructcell' string in the identity baseline, models_final.json or records_under_review.json. Distinct from bfm-chatcell (arXiv 2402.08303, zjunlp/ChatCell, chatcell-large): different paper, architecture (Q-Former + T5-base + CVAE vs ChatCell's text-only cell-sentence T5) and checkpoints. Not a rename or duplicate.

scope.note: Borderline, accepted with limits. Against: the paper says InstructCell performs on par with scBERT/scGPT/Geneformer 'despite not relying on large-scale unlabeled pre-training'; it is an instruction-tuned T5-base with new Q-Former and CVAE modules trained on 299,155 human and mouse cells from ten public datasets, and zero-shot generalization is listed only as future work. For: it releases reusable trained checkpoints (from_pretrained), spans three task families (cell-type annotation, conditional pseudo-cell generation, drug-sensitivity prediction) across two species and multiple tissues, and adds new modules, so it is neither a single-task predictor nor a thin fine-tune. The displayed catalog already includes the same group's ChatCell and CellWhisperer as singlecell language-cell models, so inclusion follows precedent. Modality singlecell matches that precedent (text + scRNA-seq). The record must state that it is instruction-tuned without large-scale single-cell pretraining.

identity.note: arXiv 2311.12410 (v1 2023-11-21; arXiv metadata DOI 10.1039/D4SC00966E, journal_ref Chem. Sci. 15(22) 8380-8389, 2024), Crossref (same title, 11 authors, Chemical Science 15/22) and Europe PMC (PMID 38846388, PMC11151847) agree. The paper's Code availability section names the official artifacts: huggingface.co/insilicomedicine/nach0_base, huggingface.co/insilicomedicine/nach0_large and github.com/insilicomedicine/nach0. Both HF cards carry the arxiv:2311.12410 tag and cite DOI 10.1039/D4SC00966E. Hub org insilicomedicine = authors' company (Insilico Medicine + NVIDIA collaboration), so the release is author-endorsed. Not in the baseline (no nach0/insilico match among 444 identity rows; nearest neighbours MolT5, ChemDFM, BioT5, Galactica are different models). The insilicomedicine/nach0_pc hub repo (only .gitattributes) belongs to the separate follow-up nach0-pc (arXiv 2410.09240, point-cloud encoder) and should not be merged or aliased.

scope.note: Pretrained T5-architecture encoder-decoder (base 250M, large 780M parameters) continued-pretrained for one epoch on chemistry-filtered PubMed abstracts (13M docs), USPTO patents (119k) and ZINC molecule strings, then instruction-tuned on many tasks (biomedical NER, PICO, entailment, relation extraction, QA; property prediction, reaction/retrosynthesis, molecule generation, description-guided design). Broader than one task; not a thin fine-tune. Modality 'molecule' matches the catalog precedent for text+SMILES models (MolT5, ChemDFM); no protein/DNA input, so 'multimodal' (BioT5/Galactica precedent) is not required.

artifact.note: HF API (2026-10-10): nach0_base ungated, public, files include pytorch_model.bin, config.json, tokenizer files (Transformers T5); nach0_large ungated, public, files include nach0_large.nemo and tokenizer/spiece files (NeMo checkpoint). Both created 2024-04-29/30, last modified 2024-06-28. Correction: the proposal says no official code repository was located, but the paper names github.com/insilicomedicine/nach0; it exists (public, not archived, 0 releases), but contains only README.MD and images. The README matches the HF card body: an inference and SMILES preprocessing snippet plus NeMo usage instructions. No training code. No nach0 dataset is released under the insilicomedicine HF org (datasets: longebench, CREED, URSA-benchmarking-sets, chemcensor, URSA-BBs); the paper says all training datasets are publicly available third-party sets. Weights not downloaded.

terms.note: Weights: both HF cards declare license cc-by-nc-4.0 in metadata, and the card text narrows this further: 'all model weights are exclusively licensed for research purposes'. Code: GitHub repo has no licence file (GitHub licence API 404; repo license null), so the README snippet is all rights reserved by default. Data: the card sentence 'The accompanying dataset is licensed under CC BY 4.0, which permits solely non-commercial usage' contradicts itself, and the release has no accompanying dataset. Article: CC BY-NC 3.0 (Crossref/Europe PMC); this covers the paper only. Ungated, no API. noncommercial=true is correct. Status wording corrected to mention the unlicensed README-only repository.

terms.note: Proposal's noncommercial=false and its 'MIT code' wording are wrong or incomplete. (a) The scFoundation weights redistributed in the author Zenodo bundle are governed upstream by the scFoundation Model License: 'non-transferable, non-sublicensable, revocable ... solely for your non-commercial research purposes'; the upstream README states model-weight use is 'subject to the Model License'. The bundle's blanket CC BY 4.0 label cannot override that, so an access route carries NC terms and noncommercial must be true. (b) biollm/repo/scbert is a copy of TencentAILabHealthcare/scBERT (same file set and README), whose repository licence is GPL-3.0, so the BioLLM repository is not uniformly MIT. (c) The article's CC BY-NC-ND licence applies only to the paper text. Side finding outside this review: the baseline record bfm-scfoundation has noncommercial=false despite this upstream MODEL_LICENSE and should get its own correction.

identity.note: Paper, preprint, repo and docs are the same official project. CSBJ 35:0129 (DOI 10.34133/csbj.0129, epub 2026-06-08; Quargnali & Rivera-Fuentes, Dept. of Chemistry, University of Zurich) names https://github.com/locbp-uzh/biopipelines. The repo LICENSE copyright line is 'Gianluca Quargnali @ LOCBP ... University of Zurich' and the contributors include GianlucaQuargnali and priveraf. The bioRxiv preprint 10.64898/2026.03.11.711024 v1 (2026-03-13) has the same title and authors, and the bioRxiv API links it to the CSBJ DOI. It is not a fork. No 'biopipelines' entry (normalized name or alias) exists in fm_identity.tsv or models_final.json. Name collision: several unrelated GitHub repos are also called BioPipelines (e.g. tavareshugo/BioPipelines, wl13/BioPipelines, sdodlapati3/BioPipelines, all generic NGS scripts), so links must point to locbp-uzh.

scope.note: This is not a model. It is a Python orchestration framework: per its docs it 'does not execute computations directly' and instead generates bash scripts that run in notebooks or on clusters. It wraps many FM-class tools (RFdiffusion 1/2/3/AA, BoltzGen, ProteinMPNN/LigandMPNN, AlphaFold via ColabFold, Boltz-2, ESMFold, OpenFold3, BioEmu, DiffDock) alongside classical tools (Vina, Gnina, OpenMM, xtb, APBS, DSSP, RDKit, PyMOL). It is multi-model and broader than one task, so it fits modality 'platform' (serving/tooling hub). That matches displayed precedents Helical (Python framework wrapping FMs) and Latch Bio (workflow SDK incl. FM pipelines), and is distinct from the single-task pipelines this lane rejected (BioNeMo Structure Prediction Pipeline, T-REX). Adversarial point, not decisive: about half the integrated tools are not foundation models, and the framework hosts no models itself. The record must stay clearly labelled as a platform, not a model.

artifact.note: The access route is open MIT code on GitHub, with active releases (v1.5.2 on 2026-09-24, v1.5.3 on 2026-09-30, last push 2026-09-30, 109 stars), readthedocs documentation, Colab example notebooks and an optional MCP server. The recursive repo tree (788 entries, not truncated) bundles no model weights: the largest blobs are three executed example notebooks of 4.5 to 8.6 MB. The environments/ folder holds per-tool conda/pip specs, and weights are fetched from upstream at install or first run. The only vendored third-party code is 3Dmol.js with its own LICENSE files. Install and run were not tested.

terms.note: Framework code: MIT. The GitHub licence API reports spdx MIT for LICENSE, and the paper abstract states 'BioPipelines is available under the MIT license'. No gating, no account, no hosted API. The paper itself is CC BY 4.0. Integrated tools keep their own terms. Spot-check of the 46 tool rows in the README that link a GitHub repo, by GitHub licence API: MIT, BSD, Apache, plus copyleft (PLIP GPL-2.0, Open Babel GPL-2.0, VespaG GPL-3.0, xtb LGPL-3.0); six NOASSERTION. Of those, PLACER and RFdiffusion All-Atom LICENSE texts are BSD and cover the weights, and evolutionaryscale/esm (the link given for 'ESMFold2') LICENSE.md is MIT. The others were not read: RFdiffusion, APBS, PyMOL open-source; OpenMM returned no licence. None of the spot-checked repo licences is non-commercial. Weight terms for most tools (e.g. AlphaFold parameters, NeuralPLexer, ESMFold2) were NOT checked. noncommercial=false is therefore correct for the framework's own artifact and consistent with platform precedent (BioNeMo Agent Toolkit, Rosetta Foundry). It is not proof that every integrated route is commercially usable. README footnote: RBSDesigner2 'is not publicly available; shown for illustrative purposes'.

The paper says 'over 40 tools', but current docs say '70+ integrated tools' and the README tool table lists 86 entries, including native utilities. identity.note: Paper, repo and hub artifacts are the same model and author-endorsed. arXiv 2610.02189 (fetched via arXiv API, id_list=2610.02189; abs page HTTP 200) is 'Generative modeling of intrinsically disordered protein regions by reinforcing sparse autoencoder features', submitted 2026-10-01, Liu ... Rotskoff, abstract naming IDiom and IDiom-DB and pointing to github.com/rotskoff-group/idiom. gh api repos/rotskoff-group/idiom: fork=false, created 2026-01-22, pushed 2026-10-02, owned by the senior author's lab org; README links the same arXiv id and the jxliu2 hub collection, and the hub cards link back to the same GitHub repo and arXiv id, so the hub owner jxliu2 (first author Jason X. Liu, contact jxliu2@stanford.edu in the README) is author-endorsed, not a third-party re-upload. Baseline fm_identity.tsv has no record matching idiom/IDR/disorder/rotskoff/jxliu, so not a duplicate or rename. Note for the record: the repo documents an earlier release v0.0.0 (2026-09-09 publish date on the GitHub release, README dates it 2026-04-11) tied to an earlier workshop preprint, DOI 10.64898/2026.04.10.717777, which Crossref confirms as 'Generative design of intrinsically disordered protein regions with IDiom' (openRxiv, 2026-04-11); the proposal's single arXiv link is the current primary and this predecessor is not a separate model.

scope.note: In scope and modality 'protein' is correct. Pretrained autoregressive PLM in three sizes with released weights; README documents at least three reusable downstream routes beyond generation: unprompted and context-prompted IDR generation, sequence- and residue-level embedding extraction (model.embed, idiom_extract CLI, layer selection, mean/none/last pooling), and post-training (SFT, GRPO with custom rewards) plus SAE-based interpretability and steering. So broader than one task; it is not a single-task predictor. The domain is narrow (disordered regions only) but that is a training-distribution restriction, not a single-task artifact.

artifact.note: Weights exist as claimed; nothing downloaded. HF API: jxliu2/idiom-300M (created 2026-09-01, modified 2026-10-02) gated=false, private=false, siblings = .gitattributes, README.md, config.json, model.safetensors; jxliu2/idiom-85M and jxliu2/idiom-20M identical file sets, gated=false; jxliu2/idiomsae-300M-L18-k32 gated=false with sae.safetensors and sae_config.json. Dataset jxliu2/idiom-db gated=false, with idiom-db/idiom-db-v1_{train,validation,test}.fasta plus an idrs_only/ variant of each (card states 53,613,584 train / 270,775 validation / 270,777 test records, 54,155,136 total). GitHub release v1.0.0 (2026-10-02) carries no binary assets; install is pip from the tag, and weights pull from the hub on first use, which matches the proposal's description of the access route.

terms.note: Exact terms: code MIT (gh api repos/rotskoff-group/idiom license.spdx_id = MIT; LICENSE file body 'MIT License / Copyright (c) 2026 Rotskoff Group at Stanford University'). Weights MIT: cardData.license = mit on all three checkpoints and the SAE; the IDiom-300M card's License section states weights and code are MIT and the corpus CC BY 4.0. Corpus CC BY 4.0 (dataset cardData.license = cc-by-4.0, card front matter license: cc-by-4.0). No gating on any of the five hub repos, no API/server route, no NC term anywhere, so noncommercial=false is correct and here it is backed by named permissive licences rather than merely absent NC terms. One caveat to keep in the record rather than treat as a defect: the repo README adds 'Data examples follow the licenses of their original sources', and the corpus derives from AFDB/UniProt, so the CC BY 4.0 claim is the depositor's declaration for IDiom-DB. Status wording 'Open code + weights (MIT code and model weights; IDiom-DB corpus CC BY 4.0)' is accurate.

text.note: Factual, no inflated claims, but two wordings are loose and one documented capability is missing. (1) '19M-302M parameters' rounds the published 18.9M; the README and card tables give 18.9M / 85M / 302M, so the exact figures are preferable. (2) io and use_cases cover generation and SAE steering but omit embedding extraction and post-training (SFT/GRPO), both documented in the README with CLI entry points; including them strengthens the 'broader than one task' basis. (3) The description credits IDiom-DB as 'curated from the AlphaFold Database', matching the abstract's 'predicted IDRs'; keeping the word 'predicted' avoids implying experimentally validated disorder. RL-SAE is correctly presented as a post-training method in the paper rather than a released artifact. Year 2026 correct. No other claim in the proposed record contradicted a primary source.

text.note: Corrections. (1) The description attributes the model to BioMap only; authorship is BioMap Research plus Peking University. It also uses an 'explicitly rather than implicitly' framing and omits the key point that structure priors are used only during training, with sequence-only inference. (2) io says the masked-LM head 'requires separate training'; the card says output_layer.weight 'may be newly initialized' and MLM predictions 'may require downstream training or a matching head checkpoint'. (3) use_cases calls the rhodopsin work 'remote-homolog discovery' by ProteinSage. The paper used ProteinSage-Miner, an adapter classifier on frozen embeddings that is not released: 6 of 15 tested candidates were confirmed as proton pumps. Rephrased to embedding-based family screening. (4) The proposal's 'v2 falls in the sweep window' reasoning does not matter for inclusion: v1 (2026-03), repo (2026-07) and hub (2026-07) all predate the 2026-08-13 refresh, which missed them. Year 2026 is correct.

identity.note: arXiv 2607.20057v1 (submitted 2026-07-22, q-bio.BM) is titled 'Antigen-specific Antibody Multi-modal Foundation Model for Functional Antibody Design' (Shi, Wang, Ma, Zhang, Zheng) and its abstract names the code repo github.com/XL-S224/AAMFM. That repo calls itself 'Official implementation' of the same paper, is not a fork, owner XL-S224 lists Shanghai Jiao Tong University, and its README badge links to huggingface.co/GENTEL-Lab/AAMFM. The hub card carries the identical author list and citation and links back to the repo, so endorsement is bidirectional; GENTEL-Lab is the hub org of the GENTEL lab (SJTU, Shuangjia Zheng, last author), which the baseline already associates with github.com/GENTEL-lab (bfm-eva). A hub search for 'AAMFM' returns only GENTEL-Lab/AAMFM, so no third-party re-upload was selected. No 'aamfm' string in the identity baseline, models_final.json or records_under_review.json; distinct from bfm-esm3 (the upstream backbone, different record) and bfm-balm (unrelated antibody LM). Not a rename or duplicate.

scope.note: Pretrained and reusable: stage 1 is antibody-domain continual pretraining of an ESM3 1.4B backbone on paired antibody sequence-structure data, followed by adapter-based antigen/epitope-conditioned SFT and Cal-DPO alignment; a checkpoint plus training/generation/evaluation code are released. Modality 'protein' is correct (antibody sequence+structure conditioned on antigen structure). Breadth is the weakest criterion and I record it as a limit rather than a refutation: the paper evaluates two settings of one task family, 'De novo Antibody Sequence-Structure Co-design' (4.1) and 'Epitope-binding CDR-H3 Co-design' (4.2), plus conditioned sequence-structure representation learning; there is no released downstream-representation or property-prediction benchmark. It is not a thin fine-tune (backbone continual pretraining, not adapter-only: the 5.1M-parameter adapter is one of three stages), and it is more than a single-task predictor, but it sits near the inclusion boundary and the corrected text must not imply general-purpose antibody representation benchmarking.

artifact.note: Hub file listing (api/models/GENTEL-Lab/AAMFM?blobs=true) shows AAMFM.pt, 5,627,577,098 bytes, LFS sha256 4795a7bd...b77a1, plus README.md and .gitattributes; gated=false, private=false, disabled=false, created 2026-09-04, lastModified 2026-09-04. A HEAD on the resolve URL returns 302 to the CDN with x-linked-size 5627577098 and then 200 (no download performed, nothing executed). Size is consistent with a full fp32 1.4B-parameter trunk. Two artifact limits: (a) the card labels it only 'AAMFM model checkpoint' and does not say which stage it is (CPT, SFT or Cal-DPO), so the exact released stage is UNVERIFIED; (b) the repo has 0 GitHub releases, so the hub file is the only weight route. Inference route confirmed in code: src/eval/generate.py requires esm3_sm_open_v1.pth, esm3_structure_encoder_v0.pth, esm3_structure_decoder_v0.pth and esm3_function_decoder_v0.pth under model/base_model/esm3/data/weights and raises FileNotFoundError if absent, so the external ESM3 assets are genuinely required as the proposal claims. Training data are described as external and are not provided; the precomputed GearNet antigen features for the RAbD evaluation set are a Google Drive file (link returns HTTP 200, a Drive viewer page; no licence or terms stated there).

terms.note: Code: GitHub LICENSE file is MIT (gh api repos/XL-S224/AAMFM/license -> spdx MIT, path LICENSE). Weights: hub cardData license 'mit' and the card's License section states the checkpoint and the source-code repository are released under MIT. One real tension the proposal did not surface: the repository README's License section is narrower - code MIT, while 'Pretrained model weights, external datasets, and third-party tools remain subject to their respective licenses and terms'. Read against the hub card, this most plausibly refers to the external ESM3 weights and data rather than AAMFM.pt, but the two author statements are not identical and the corrected status must name the carve-out instead of flattening both to 'MIT checkpoint'. Upstream terms, which the proposal explicitly left unread, I read: github.com/evolutionaryscale/esm LICENSE.md is MIT verbatim, and huggingface.co/api/models/EvolutionaryScale/esm3-sm-open-v1 redirects (307) to biohub/esm3-sm-open-v1, which is gated=false and whose card states 'This repository is under a MIT license'. So the required base weights add no non-commercial or gating restriction and noncommercial=false survives my attempt to refute it. Residual unverified terms: the Google Drive antigen-feature file (no stated licence) and the training data (external, unspecified); US-align is an optional third-party evaluation tool under its own terms. Flagged not-ok only because the proposal's status/audit_note wording is inaccurate (leaves the ESM3 terms open and omits the README carve-out), not because a prohibited term was found.

urls.note: All three URLs in the proposed record fetched by me today and each shows what its label says: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20057 (via export.arxiv.org id_list query, HTTP 200, one entry, matching title/authors/date) labelled arXiv; https://github.com/XL-S224/AAMFM (gh api, HTTP 200, MIT, created 2026-07-22, pushed 2026-09-04, 19 stars) labelled GitHub; https://huggingface.co/GENTEL-Lab/AAMFM (api + raw README, HTTP 200, ungated, AAMFM.pt present) labelled Hugging Face. Also fetched and consistent: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.20057 (HTTP 200, full text).

text.note: Two defects. (1) Misattribution: the proposed io ('... and pseudo-log-likelihood scores') and use_cases ('design candidate scoring') present PLL as an AAMFM output. The paper computes PLL with AntiBERTy, a third-party antibody language model, as a plausibility constraint and evaluation metric ('we introduce pseudo-log-likelihood (PLL) under the antibody language model AntiBERTy ... as a sequence-level plausibility constraint'; Metrics: 'the pseudo-log-likelihood (Pll) calculated by AntiBERTy'), and the repo utility is src/eval/compute_pll.py, docstring 'Recompute AntiBERTy PLL metrics from an antibody generation CSV.' PLL removed from io and use_cases in the corrected record. (2) Status/audit_note left the external ESM3 terms unresolved ('were not read here') and omitted the repository README licence carve-out; both corrected. Otherwise factual: description matches the paper's three-stage pipeline and the ESM3 1.4B backbone ('We use ESM-3 (version 3.1.6) as the base model, specifically the open-source 1.4B parameter version', A.4); year 2026 matches the preprint (Jul 2026) and checkpoint upload (Sep 2026); alias matches the paper title; no inflated performance claim is carried into the record text.

Caveat the proposal did not state: the paper's Code availability statement names only the main lareaulab/Trias checkpoint, not lareaulab/Trias-Small; endorsement of the second checkpoint rests on same-org ownership plus the Trias-Small card's cross-link to the main card, and the paper's description of 'Trias-small' (12.3M parameters, mammalian-only) matches that checkpoint's config (d_model 256, 4 heads, ffn 1024) versus Trias (d_model 512, 8 heads, ffn 2048).

scope.note: In scope. Pretrained BART-style encoder-decoder, 47M parameters per the paper, trained on 10 million coding sequences from 640 vertebrate species (NCBI RefSeq), max 2,046 tokens. Reusable beyond one task: species-conditioned generation (greedy / beam / nucleus decoding) plus zero-shot likelihood scoring that the paper correlates with measured mRNA stability and protein output across independent datasets; the paper also uses encoder embeddings for interpretation. Modality 'rna' is correct (codon/CDS sequence model, not protein structure or DNA regulatory). Not a single-task predictor and not a thin fine-tune: weights are trained from scratch on the authors' own corpus. Trias-Small is a smaller, separately trained mammalian variant sharing paper, code and terms, so recording it as an alias rather than a second record is defensible.

text.note: Three wording problems, all correctable, none affecting the accept decision. (1) io 'Target RNA length or conditioning scaffold -> ...' and use_cases listing 'scaffold-conditioned inverse folding' read as released functionality; the released sampler takes --num_res (plus seed/device/output) and the README and HF card state that the commands do sampling only. (2) status and audit_note say 'released structure dataset' / 'released training corpus' without saying it is the 10,631-structure trRosettaRNA2 subset, not the 168,561-structure corpus. (3) audit_note says 'Part of the released training corpus consists of predicted rather than experimental structures'; the paper's Limitations say 'most of our corpus consists of predicted or synthetic structures', so the note understates the gap. Everything else is factual: 168,561-structure corpus, 10,631 MSA-supported structures generated by the authors, two variants differing in triangle pair updates (Base no pair updates, Tri every 2 blocks), latent dim 16, 12 flow layers, all-heavy-atom PDB output, year 2026, aliases La-Ribo-Base / La-Ribo-Tri. identity.note: arXiv 2609.38908v1 (submitted 2026-09-30; Zhao, Liu, Luo, Nie; primary q-bio.GN) links https://github.com/PharMolix/CellMSA in the abstract. Both repo commits are authored by Suyuan Zhao (first author). PharMolix is the GitHub account (type User, not Organization) that also hosts the baseline records LangCell, SToFM and OpenBioMed (BioMedGPT/PharMolixFM/MolFM), so the repo is author-official. The first commit is an empty root commit titled 'Withdraw initial CellMSA publication'; the second (2026-09-29) adds the code, checkpoint and demo. No Hugging Face artifact (search 'CellMSA' empty; PharMolix HF models do not include it), so no third-party re-upload concern. Not a duplicate: normalized name 'cellmsa' and the repo URL are absent from the baseline; nearest name collisions (GPN-MSA, MSA Transformer, MSA Pairformer) are DNA/protein models; LangCell is an earlier, different model by the same first author.

scope.note: Pretrained single-cell representation model: one epoch on ~109M human CELLxGENE cell observations (65.6M primary; 2,090 datasets, 818 cell types) with three objectives (masked expression, reconstruction, contrastive). The released checkpoint is used zero-shot as an embedding model for batch integration, cell type/state classification (MLP head) and perturbation prediction (with STATE-ST). Broader than one task; modality singlecell is correct. Reuse caveat: inference needs a reference AnnData plus precomputed context-cell indices for each query cell. The shipped context script and demo are label-informed (they need cell_type, donor_id and supertype annotations), and the notebook says so explicitly. The paper's label-free HVG-PCA-KNN retrieval is not shipped as a script; users can supply generic obsm['neighbor_indices'] themselves.

artifact.note: best_model.pt is a Git LFS pointer (oid sha256:893f24da..., size 566247092). The GitHub LFS batch API returns a download action for that oid (no error). A HEAD request on the media.githubusercontent.com URL returned 200 with content-length 566247092; weights were not downloaded. README says the checkpoint holds the model weights and gene vocabulary. The demo data (blood_subset.h5ad, precomputed embeddings .npy) are also LFS objects. No releases, no API or server, no pretraining-corpus release (the corpus is drawn from public CELLxGENE).

identity.note: Paper (bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.09.22.753590, posted 2026-09-28, corresponding author Hongpeng Zhou, University of Manchester) names github.com/UoM-HealthAI/NexuST and huggingface.co/Haiping-UoM/NexuST in Code availability; the HF card and GitHub README both cite the same DOI and author list (first author Haiping Liu). Repo is not a fork, created 2026-09-22; HF repo created 2026-09-22. Author-endorsed, not a third-party re-upload. Not a duplicate: no baseline name/alias/URL match for nexust or HiGeST (internal wandb project name in README). Closest baseline record is bfm-cellworld (same group, same HF account, same 46M-cell corpus; HumanST-46M card mentions the 'CellWorld memory-mapped representation'), but CellWorld is a distinct model: latent-space JEPA-style prediction, four variants 5.74M-94.56M parameters, separate arXiv paper, repo and hub repo. NexuST uses masked gene-value reconstruction with 67.9M parameters (60.6M encoder). Separate record is justified; the relationship should be stated in audit_note.

scope.note: Pretrained (10,000-step masked gene-value reconstruction on HumanST-46M) and reusable: repo ships embedding inference (inference.py / nexust-embed), frozen linear probing and full fine-tuning for cell annotation, region prediction, gene recovery, niche and density tasks, plus pretraining code. Broader than one task. Modality 'spatial' is correct under MAINTENANCE.md (spatial transcriptomics routes to spatial, consistent with Nicheformer, scGPT-spatial, CellWorld); found in the singlecell lane but correctly cross-routed.

artifact.note: HF model API: gated=false, private=false; tree lists NexuST-step10000.ckpt, 815,205,507 bytes, LFS sha256 178de8d6...7d7e, matching the size and SHA256 stated on the card. Paper trains for exactly 10,000 steps, so this is the end-of-pretraining state; the card says it is not the separately saved best-validation-loss checkpoint, and the paper does not say which checkpoint the reported results used (my search of the full text found no statement). Card says a verified loading example is not in the hub repo, but the GitHub README gives inference, probe and fine-tune commands that load checkpoints/NexuST-step10000.ckpt. No GitHub releases. Weights not downloaded or executed.

terms.note: Code: MIT (LICENSE file, GitHub API spdx MIT, pyproject license = {file = LICENSE}). Data: HumanST-46M HF dataset is ungated with no licence; its card says licence terms will be documented separately; upstream vendor/academic source terms not checked. Paper: CC BY 4.0. No API/server. No NC terms found on any route, so noncommercial=false is consistent, but it is not a permissive grant. Proposed status wording ('without stated weight licence') should say explicitly that weights are all rights reserved by default and should cover the data. identity.note: Cell Reports Methods article 101612 (Crossref: Cao S, Yang K, Cheng J, Li J, Shen H-B, Pan X, Yuan Y; Sept 2026; Europe PMC PMID 42815472, first pub 2026-09-30), bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.09.27.615337 (same authors, v1 2024-09-29, v7 2025-08-04), GitHub csh3/stFormer (not a fork; LICENSE copyright Shenghao Cao & Ye Yuan, SJTU; README cites the DOI) and Zenodo 20755048 (creator Cao, Shenghao; related identifier isPublishedIn the DOI) are one author-endorsed model. No match in the baseline by name, normalized name, csh3, Zenodo IDs or DOI; no hold record. No Hugging Face copies found. Unrelated 'STFormer' models (EEG, video segmentation, histology-to-ST prediction) exist; aliases stay empty.

scope.note: Pretrained transformer (scFoundation-initialised gene embeddings + biased cross-attention to niche ligand genes) on ~4.1M samples from deconvolved public human Visium sections; reused for cell clustering, batch-effect correction, cell type prediction, gene function prediction and in silico ligand-receptor perturbation. Broader than one task. Modality spatial matches spatial-transcriptomics precedent (Nicheformer, Novae).

artifact.note: Author README: pretrained weights (pretraining/), fine-tuned weights (tasks/fine-tuning_mse) and formatted data are in Zenodo 20755048. Zenodo API: open, MIT label, files stFormer.tar.gz (9,342,911,432 B) + case_studies.tar.gz (408,606,333 B); HEAD on the tarball returns 200. The same 9.3 GB tarball has been public since Zenodo version 16731623 (2025-08-04). A bounded 4 MB range read (headers listed only, nothing extracted or kept) shows a repo snapshot (stFormer/README.md, LICENSE, tasks/...) dated Aug 2025; the pretraining/ entries were not reached, so the checkpoint pretraining/models/model_4.1M.ckpt that the task notebooks load is documented by the authors but was not seen directly. GitHub release v1.0 (2026-08-21) has no assets. Limitation: it is a single 9.3 GB bundle with data and figures, not a standalone checkpoint, and building the model also requires the separately downloaded scFoundation checkpoint (BioMap SharePoint link in tasks/scfoundation/models/download.txt).

terms.note: Proposal is wrong on NC. Code: MIT (GitHub). Zenodo deposit: labelled MIT, open. But the paper states the gene lookup-table embeddings 'are initialized by those from the scFoundation model' and the value encoder is 'borrowed from scFoundation'; pretraining.py and the task notebooks build the model by loading scfoundation/models/models.ckpt and copying its token/position embeddings. scFoundation weights are licensed 'solely for your non-commercial research purposes' (BioMap MODEL_LICENSE; a copy ships in stFormer's tasks/scfoundation/MODEL_LICENSE.txt). An access route therefore carries NC terms, so noncommercial must be true; the MIT label on the archive cannot be read as a permissive licence for scFoundation-derived parameters. Pretraining corpus: on request only. No API/server. Journal article VOR: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (Crossref); preprint: no-reuse (bioRxiv 'cc_no'); these are text licences, not model terms.

urls.note: doi.org/10.1016/j.crmeth.2026.101612 -> 302 to linkinghub.elsevier.com (200, redirect page to cell.com; cell.com full text 403 to automated fetch, metadata confirmed via Crossref/Europe PMC). bioRxiv v1 landing 200 with matching title. github.com/csh3/stFormer 200 with matching title. zenodo.org/records/20755048 200 (default UA; 403 with a browser UA) with matching title and MIT label. GitHub blob pages were rate-limited (503/429) during the check; the same files were read through the GitHub API (200).

text.note: Description omits the scFoundation initialisation, which matters for both identity and terms; '4.1 million spatial samples' is the paper's wording but they are deconvolved cell-level samples from 432 sections in 75 Visium datasets (preprint v7). use_cases 'Spatial clustering ... fine-tuned spatial prediction tasks' is vague and partly inflated; replaced with the tasks the paper and repo actually report. Status 'Open code + weights (MIT; Zenodo archive)' hides the NC dependency and on-request pretraining data. io wording tightened (gene embeddings + max-pooled cell embedding). Year 2024 = first public preprint, consistent with the scGPT precedent (both links listed); note that Nicheformer/scFoundation use the journal year, so the catalog convention is mixed.

identity.note: The arXiv paper 2508.16085 (v1 22 Aug 2025, v2 7 Aug 2026) and the Cancer Cell article (DOI 10.1016/j.ccell.2026.08.008, PMID 42721959, PMCID PMC13564370; Crossref and Europe PMC agree) have the same title and authors. Both cite github.com/lilab-stanford/ELF as the official code. The GitHub README links huggingface.co/luoxd96/ELF as 'Pretrained inference weights'. That Hub account belongs to Xiangde Luo, the first author; the 20 Aug 2026 commit is by Xiangde Luo from a stanford.edu host, and the model card links back to arXiv and GitHub. So the Hub repo is endorsed by the authors and is not a third-party re-upload. Caveat: the paper's own weight link (Data and code availability, Key resources table) points to a Google Drive file named checkpoint_best.pth, a training checkpoint. The Hub repo instead holds an inference-only extraction. The paper says 'ELF contains only 14.3 million (M) parameters', but the Hub config.json lists n_params 151304. The Hub layers (interpolate, LayerNorm, 8 gated ABMIL heads of width 96) match the paper's Methods exactly, so the gap is probably training-only modules. That is not proven, and I did not check equivalence with the Drive checkpoint because it would require downloading weights. Baseline: no ELF name, alias or URL appears in fm_identity.tsv. bfm-musk (the same lab's MUSK) is a different model, and COBRA, which the paper uses as a comparator, has no record.

scope.note: ELF is a slide-level encoder pretrained with MoCo v3 contrastive learning plus auxiliary weak supervision (cancer vs normal, organ) on 53,699 WSIs from 11 public datasets covering 20 anatomical sites. It outputs general slide embeddings that are evaluated by linear probing on classification, biomarker and therapy-response tasks, so it is not a single-task predictor. It belongs to the same class as the catalogued slide encoders TITAN, CHIEF and PRISM. The modality 'spatial' (pathology) is correct. Adversarial note: the released encoder is a small aggregator (about 151k parameters) and is not a standalone image model. It needs pre-extracted tile features from five third-party encoders. The record must keep saying this, and it does.

artifact.note: The Hugging Face API for luoxd96/ELF returns gated=false and private=false, with createdAt 2026-08-20. Files: elf_slide_encoder.pth (621,629 bytes), config.json, modeling_elf.py, README.md, requirements.txt. The GitHub repo (35 tree entries) has pretrain, inference and evaluation code but no weights and no releases. The paper-linked Google Drive view page resolves and shows the filename checkpoint_best.pth; the size is not shown and the file was not downloaded. The README also links Google Drive folders of precomputed evaluation embeddings; these were not checked.

terms.note: Neither the GitHub repo nor the Hub repo has a LICENSE file: gh api /license returns 404 and the tree contains no licence or COPYING file. The terms appear only in prose. The GitHub README says 'This code is made available under the GPLv3 License and is available for non-commercial academic purposes.' The Hub card table says 'GPLv3, non-commercial academic use', and the Hub metadata says gpl-3.0. GPLv3 plus a non-commercial restriction is internally inconsistent, so the record should treat it as non-commercial (the same precedent as bfm-chief), and noncommercial=true is correct. The Google Drive checkpoint page shows no terms. CORRECTION: the proposed status calls the required tile encoders 'partly gated', but the Hugging Face API shows all five are gated (gated=auto). UNI, CONCH v1.5 and Virchow2 are cc-by-nc-nd-4.0; Prov-GigaPath and H-optimus-0 are apache-2.0. The pretraining WSIs come from public datasets, each with its own terms.

urls.note: All four record URLs resolve and match their labels. arxiv.org/abs/2508.16085 returns 200. doi.org/10.1016/j.ccell.2026.08.008 returns 302 to linkinghub.elsevier.com (200); Crossref gives the container-title 'Cancer Cell'. github.com/lilab-stanford/ELF returns 200, and huggingface.co/luoxd96/ELF returns 200. In the corrected record I added the PMC full-text URL and the paper-linked Google Drive weight URL to sources, and fetched both (200).

text.note: Corrections: (1) Year: change 2025 to 2026. The catalog uses the journal year when a journal version exists (PRISM2: arXiv 2025, record 2026; TITAN: arXiv 2024, record 2025; UNI and CONCH: arXiv 2023, record 2024), and Cancer Cell is 2026. (2) Description: 'five public pathology foundation models' becomes 'five third-party' encoders, because all five are gated. The new wording also adds the MoCo v3 plus weak-supervision pretraining and the concatenation ensemble from the Methods. (3) io: add CLAM 10x tile features and the per-model native/768-d outputs (Hub card, modeling_elf.py). (4) Status: fix the gating wording, state that no licence file exists, and mention the Google Drive training checkpoint. (5) audit_note: record the gap between 14.3M and 151,304 parameters. Also, the journal text has now been read through the PMC full text, so 'journal page itself was not fetched' no longer applies. The use_cases claims trace to the paper's results sections, and none is inflated.

identity.note: Closed provenance loop: arXiv 2506.11152 (first author Hiren Madhu; Ying/Krishnaswamy labs) states code at github.com/Graph-and-Geometric-Learning/HEIST; that repo's README points to the HirenMadhu Hugging Face account and loads 'HirenMadhu/HEIST'; utils/inference.py hard-codes HF_REPO = "HirenMadhu/HEIST"; the HF card links back to the GitHub repo. All HF commits by HirenMadhu (first author). Not a third-party re-upload. No HEIST, arXiv ID, GitHub org or HF account match in baseline fm_identity.tsv (400 displayed + 44 held); only FM-tree hit is this run's own candidate_decisions.json copy of the proposal. Alias 'Hierarchical Embeddings for Integrated Spatial Transcriptomics' comes from the author HF card only (paper title does not expand the acronym). ICLR 2026 venue is claimed by README/card BibTeX but OpenReview was not readable (307 redirect / challenge) -> venue UNVERIFIED; record does not claim it.

scope.note: Pretrained hierarchical graph transformer (spatially-aware contrastive + masked autoencoding) evaluated frozen/zero-shot and fine-tuned on four downstream tasks (cell clustering, cell type annotation, clinical outcome prediction, gene imputation) across spatial transcriptomics and proteomics. Broader than one task; reusable embedding encoder. Modality 'spatial' matches comparable records (Nicheformer, scGPT-spatial, Novae).

artifact.note: HF API (2026-10-10): gated=false, private=false; siblings HEIST.pth (126,062,091 B), model.safetensors (41,707,072 B) + config.json at root (v1), v2.0/gene_vocab.json, v2.0/marker_xenium/{config.json, model.safetensors 45,033,192 B}. Commits: v1 uploaded 2026-04-24; 'Add HEIST v2.0 models: marker_xenium' 2026-10-08. Card lists v2.0/marker_all and v2.0/nomarker_all, which are NOT in the file listing. Correction needed: the code default in embed.py and load_heist() is "v2.0/marker_all", so default-argument inference points to a checkpoint that is not uploaded; users must pass v1 or v2.0/marker_xenium. Material caveat the proposal under-weights: the author card states v1 (the paper-era checkpoint) was trained on data with a preprocessing bug 'where every cell of a cell type shared one gene-expression vector'; arXiv v4 (2026-06-04) does not mention it. No GitHub releases or tags; repo contains no checkpoint files (hub is the weight route). Weights not downloaded.

Code: gh api /license -> 404, recursive tree (66 blobs) has no LICENSE/COPYING/NOTICE anywhere incl. mioflow_heist/; README 'License' section states CC BY 4.0 for 'This work'. arXiv full text is CC BY 4.0. Pretraining data are public 10x/Vizgen/SEA-AD sources re-fetched by data_prep scripts, not redistributed. text.note: Corrections: (1) description attributed '~22 million cells' to the model generally; that is the v1/paper corpus (22.3M cells, 124 tissue slices, 15 organs, 13.3M 10x + 8.7M Vizgen + 360K SEA-AD). v2.0 uses a rebuilt Xenium/Vizgen/SEA-AD corpus of unstated size and a 6,495-gene human vocabulary. The v1 preprocessing bug disclosed by the authors must be stated. (2) use_cases listed 'niche annotation' and 'embedding visualisation' and omitted gene imputation; the paper's four tasks are cell clustering, cell type annotation, clinical outcome prediction, gene imputation; niches appear only as attention analysis. (3) Proteomics transfer is a paper (v1) result; v2 marker models ignore genes outside the human gene vocabulary, so proteomics-panel transfer for v2 is undocumented. (4) Year 2025 (arXiv v1) correct. (5) Added required schema fields (id, date_added, canonical, verified, audit_priority, audit_source) following 2026-09-11 addition conventions (canonical false, P3, verified_with_limits).
